contract.settlement_definition: KXNHLOT settles YES iff at least one overtime period actually commences in the single listed NHL game, i.e. the regulation score is level after 60:00 and the opening faceoff of OT is taken; the market is binary with floor_strike 0.5. Goals, shootout outcome and who wins are irrelevant to settlement. Postponed games stay open if they begin within 48h, otherwise the market resolves to a fair price. KXNHL2OT (double overtime) and KXNHLSERIESOT (series overtime) currently list no markets, so their settlement text is unseen. Source of truth is the official NHL game record.

rules_evidence.quote: play in that overtime period commences, meaning that the opening faceoff of that overtime period is taken
rules_evidence.establishes: The event is the overtime faceoff, not an overtime goal: a tie after 60 minutes is necessary and sufficient, so the target is P(regulation tie) incl. empty-net goals.

rules_evidence.quote: If the game is postponed but begins within 48 hours of its originally scheduled start time, the market will remain open
rules_evidence.establishes: Postponement within 48h keeps the contract live; beyond that it resolves to a fair price (a void-like outcome), so late postponements truncate exposure rather than resolve NO.

variants_and_edge_cases: Regular season vs playoffs: in the regular season OT is one 5-minute 3v3 period then a shootout; in the playoffs OT periods are 20-minute 5v5 sudden death, so KXNHL2OT (title only) only exists in the playoffs and is a conditional on a first OT with no goal.
A scheduled or announced OT in which no faceoff happens does not count; a goal at 60:00 ends regulation so the faceoff-defined event excludes games decided by a goal in the final seconds.
KXNHLSERIESOT has no listed markets: it is unknown whether it counts the number of OT games in a series, any OT game in the series, or a specific game; marked CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS.

BTTS, shootout, first-goal and early-goal families appear in this archetype's blueprint but have no live KXNHLOT-style series here; the only live early-goal series (KXNHLF10G) is filed under the player archetype.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official NHL game record (period scores, OT flag) as published on nhl.com / the NHL stats API; Kalshi settles from the league result.

mechanism.summary: An overtime market is a binary on the event that regulation ends level. Mechanically: two teams draw regulation goal counts from correlated, mildly overdispersed processes whose means come from shot volume x shot quality x opposing goalie, plus special-teams goals; the tie probability is the diagonal of the joint score distribution, so it rises as the expected total falls and as the expected goal difference approaches zero. Superimposed on that is a late-game control process: a trailing team pulls its goalie, which raises the chance of an equalizer but also of a 2-goal loss via an empty-net goal, so the diagonal mass is moved by coaching policy and score state in the last 3-5 minutes. Only the regulation end state matters; what happens in OT is irrelevant for KXNHLOT but decisive for the double-OT and shootout siblings. Season type (regular vs playoff) shifts rates, and standings stakes may change late risk-taking when a tied game guarantees a point.

stages.name: Regulation scoring means and the joint score distribution
stages.description: For each side, expected regulation goals = attempts x share that are on goal x goal probability per shot (xG, finishing, opposing goalie) summed over 5v5, PP and PK states, with PP time driven by penalties. The pair (H, A) is not independent: pace, penalty counts and game state make the goal counts weakly positively correlated early and negatively correlated late (leader sits, trailer presses). The tie probability is sum_k P(H=k, A=k) and is a convex function of the expected total and bell-shaped in the goal-difference mean; mis-specified dispersion misprices the 1-1, 2-2 and 3-3 cells most.
stages.distribution: Overdispersed bivariate count (negative-binomial or Poisson-mixture) with game-state-dependent correlation; tie mass concentrated on 2-2 and 3-3 with a thin right tail.

stages.name: Starting goalie and lineup shock before puck drop
stages.description: The expected goals of both teams move by roughly a tenth to a third of a goal when the confirmed starter differs from the presumed one or a top-line forward or top-pair defenceman is out. Because the tie probability depends on the total and on the gap, a goalie change on the weaker side can raise or lower P(tie) depending on whether it closes the gap or lifts the total, so the sign of the effect is not fixed. Confirmation arrives 1-3 hours before puck drop, so the information vintage at trading time matters.
stages.distribution: Discrete mixture over starter identity (2-3 states per team) with different mean goals; each mixture component has its own tie probability and the market price is the weighted mixture.

stages.name: Late-regulation control: pulled goalie, equalizer and empty-net goals
stages.description: In the last 2-5 minutes a trailing team replaces its goalie; the 6v5 state raises the trailing team's scoring rate several-fold but exposes it to empty-net goals at a much higher rate than it scores. A one-goal deficit is converted to a tie with a modest probability or to a two-goal loss with a larger one, and the coach's pull time and the standings value of a loser point change the policy. Level games late may see more conservative play. Net effect: late dynamics move mass between the diagonal (ties) and +/-2 margins, so a team-specific pull policy changes P(OT) beyond what the 60-minute rates imply.
stages.distribution: Regime switch at about 3 minutes left in a one-goal game; equalizer success is a low-probability Bernoulli (order of 15-25 percent of pulls) whose rate is team- and coach-specific.

stages.name: Settlement mapping: overtime commenced, season type and series structure
stages.description: The contract pays when the opening faceoff of OT occurs, so the settlement variable is simply the tie indicator at 60:00. For playoff-only siblings the second OT adds the conditional that a 20-minute 5v5 sudden-death period passed without a goal, a hazard that depends on 5v5 tied-state rates and fatigue; for the series contract the games in a series share team strength, goalies and coaching so OT occurrence is positively dependent across games. Postponement beyond 48h converts to a fair-price settlement, not a loss.
stages.distribution: Tie indicator is Bernoulli with p about 0.22-0.27 in the regular season; double-OT conditional is geometric in the 20-minute hazard; series OT count is beta-binomial rather than binomial.

environment.note: Rinks are indoors so weather is irrelevant, rink scoring factors enter through team home/away ratings, and the tie indicator is insensitive to small venue shifts in shot counting.

nhl.third_period_equalizer_hazard.label: Late-game equalizer and empty-net hazard by team and coach
nhl.third_period_equalizer_hazard.mechanism: Converts a one-goal late deficit into tie or two-goal-loss outcomes using 6v5 rates and the coach's pull time.
nhl.third_period_equalizer_hazard.rationale: The existing empty_net input is a single bucket for 'pulled-goalie timing'; for tie probability the two competing outcomes of a pull (equalizer vs empty-net goal against) and their dependence on pull time are what move the diagonal of the score distribution. Pull time has drifted earlier league-wide and differs by coach.
nhl.third_period_equalizer_hazard.measurement: From play-by-play, for every regular-season and playoff game since 2015-16 find states with the trailing team down exactly one goal and the goalie pulled; per team-coach compute (a) median pull time in seconds remaining, (b) equalizer rate = goals for per 60 minutes of 6v5 time, (c) empty-net goals against per 60 of 6v5 time. Shrink each to league with k=20 pulls, weight seasons with 2-year half-life, and reset on a coaching change. Output pregame P(equalizer | trailing by 1 at T-3:00) and P(EN | trailing by 1) per team pair.
free_sources: NHL API play-by-play (situationCode and event times)
raw_data: play-by-play events: period, clock, strength situationCode, goalie-in-net flag, goal events
coach by game
nhl.third_period_equalizer_hazard.why: Directly sets P(tie at 60:00) beyond the 55-minute state; two teams with identical 60-minute ratings but different pull policy get different OT probabilities.

nhl.ot_sudden_death_hazard_5v5.label: 5v5 sudden-death overtime goal hazard (playoff OT)
nhl.ot_sudden_death_hazard_5v5.mechanism: Hazard of a goal per 20-minute playoff overtime period at 5v5 given tied score, fatigue and style.
nhl.ot_sudden_death_hazard_5v5.rationale: Playoff overtime is 5v5 sudden death in 20-minute periods, not the 3v3 of the regular season, so the existing 3v3 rate does not transfer; double-OT markets depend on the first period producing no goal, which has a different hazard than 60-minute rates imply.
nhl.ot_sudden_death_hazard_5v5.measurement: Pool all playoff OT minutes since 2005-06 (about 450 games) at 5v5 and compute the goal rate per 60 for tied score; model hazard h(t) = h0 x tied-game 5v5 multiplier x team-pair factor, where the team-pair factor is the geometric mean of both teams' tied 5v5 xG rate shrunk to league with k=500 minutes. Fatigue multiplier estimated from period index (OT1 vs OT2) and rest differential. P(no goal in OT1) = exp(-h x 20/60). Do not use regular-season 3v3 minutes.
raw_data: playoff OT play-by-play: elapsed OT seconds, strength, goal time
team tied-state 5v5 xG rates
nhl.ot_sudden_death_hazard_5v5.why: Needed for the KXNHL2OT sibling (no listed markets now): that market is a conditional on a goalless first OT.

nhl.series_ot_count_dependence.label: Within-series dependence of overtime occurrence
nhl.series_ot_count_dependence.mechanism: Intraclass correlation of per-game tie indicators within the same playoff series.
nhl.series_ot_count_dependence.rationale: Games in one series share goalies, coaches and defensive structure, so OT counts are overdispersed relative to independent Bernoulli; a binomial series-OT price is too thin-tailed.
nhl.series_ot_count_dependence.measurement: Fit a beta-binomial to the count of games reaching OT in each historical playoff series (2005-06 onward, series lengths 4-7 handled by conditioning on length), estimate overdispersion rho; then per series set p_game = reg_tie_model pregame tie probability and apply rho to get the pmf of OT-game count. Update rho with a prior of 0.05 and k=40 series.
raw_data: series_id, game number, period scores, OT flag
nhl.series_ot_count_dependence.why: Only series-level OT contracts need it; those series are not currently listed, so it is a gap-closing input rather than an active signal.

nhl.tied_late_risk_posture.label: Tied-game closing posture (late risk aversion when a point is banked)
nhl.tied_late_risk_posture.mechanism: Change in late 5v5 attempt share and danger in tied games relative to earlier tied-game play.
nhl.tied_late_risk_posture.rationale: A tied third period guarantees a standings point, which may lower risk-taking; if present it raises P(OT) above what 60-minute rates give. It is a hypothesis to measure, not an assumed effect.
nhl.tied_late_risk_posture.measurement: For each team and season compute shot-attempt share and high-danger attempts per 60 at 5v5 in the final 5:00 of regulation when the score is tied, minus the same team's rate in minutes 40:00-55:00 when tied; shrink to league with k=60 tied-late minutes and report per-team posture index; interact with standings leverage (points pct within 4 of a cutoff). Add the minimum of two teams' indices as the pair posture.
free_sources: Natural Stat Trick score-and-time filtered splits
raw_data: 5v5 attempts and danger events by clock and score
standings points percentage by date
nhl.tied_late_risk_posture.why: Tests whether level late games under-produce regulation goals relative to the tie model.

nhl.reg_tie_model.reason: Correct core object for KXNHLOT (settles on the diagonal of the regulation score); must be fit on post-empty-net regulation scores and conditioned on total and spread rather than on any market price.

nhl.total_goal_dispersion.reason: Parameterises the same bivariate model as reg_tie_model (variance, correlation) rather than adding an independent signal; keep as a hyperparameter block, not a separate primary feature.

nhl.game_script_prob.reason: Win probability is the wrong summary for a tie event: tie mass depends on the absolute goal gap and total, not on who is favoured; also derived from the same ratings so it adds little beyond xG pair.

nhl.ot_3v3_rate.reason: Irrelevant to KXNHLOT (settles at the OT faceoff) but needed by the shootout and multi-OT siblings; the 3v3 rate also does not describe playoff 5v5 overtime.

nhl.shootout_record.reason: Shootout skill is near coin-flip noise and only affects who wins after OT; neither KXNHLOT nor any listed event depends on it.

nhl.playoff_context.reason: Regime flag that changes overtime format, scoring rates and which siblings exist; needed because playoff tie rates and OT lengths differ structurally.

nhl.xg_for.reason: Feeds each side's mean but the OT event depends only on the pair (total, gap); BTTS role named in the draft has no live series here, so secondary not primary.

nhl.xg_against.reason: Same pair-level use as xg_for; the matchup combination of the two teams' xG for/against matters, not either alone.

nhl.goalie_start.reason: A starter swap shifts total and gap by tenths of a goal, moving P(tie) by a point or two; the 'shutout probability' rationale belongs to BTTS which has no live contract.

nhl.goalie_quality.reason: Enters through expected goals against and total; shrunk GSAx has low persistence, so influence on tie probability is small.

nhl.first_goal_hazard.reason: First-goal timing does not change whether the game is tied at 60:00; the live early-goal series is filed elsewhere, so this input is mis-attached to the OT contract.

nhl.opening_shift_deployment.reason: Who starts the first shift has negligible effect on a 60-minute tie indicator; relevant only to early-goal windows.

nhl.penalty_rates.reason: Penalties move expected total modestly; their effect on the tie indicator flows only through the mean, so the text about early PP and first goals does not apply.

nhl.empty_net.reason: Mislabelled secondary: empty-net goals and pulls convert one-goal leads to two-goal wins and trailing deficits to ties, i.e. they directly move the diagonal mass.

m.rules_text.reason: The faceoff-based definition of 'played' and the 48h postponement rule are only visible in the text and define the target event.

m.strike_hit_rates.reason: Kalshi settled-frequency history is an outcome of this market, not a cause; the regulation tie rate should instead be computed from 20 years of NHL results.

nhl.pdo_regression.reason: PDO regression refines team strength but tie probability is insensitive to small strength shifts once the total and gap are set.

nhl.finishing.reason: Finishing talent is already folded into xG-to-goals conversion in team ratings; its marginal effect on P(tie) is tiny and hard to separate from PDO.

interactions.mechanism: Tie probability is a joint function of the expected total and the expected gap: for a given gap it falls roughly with the square root of the total, and for a given total it peaks at gap zero; neither alone prices the diagonal.
interactions.how_to_test: Bin historical games by (expected total, expected gap) and compare realised tie rate with the product of marginal tie rates at each bin; test a gap x total interaction term.

interactions.mechanism: Below roughly three minutes with a one-goal deficit the process flips to 6v5; the same trailing team can produce an equalizer (adds to ties) or an empty-net goal against (removes the tie path), so the sign of the pull effect depends on the coach's pull time and on the team's 6v5 conversion.
interactions.how_to_test: Split one-goal-deficit states at 3:00 left by team pull policy tercile and compare realised tie-at-60 frequency across terciles after controlling for 55-minute score.

interactions.mechanism: Season type switches the overtime generator: 3v3 five-minute period then shootout in the regular season versus unlimited 20-minute 5v5 periods in the playoffs; the 3v3 rate must not be used for playoff double-OT hazard.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit OT goal hazard separately by season type and test whether team 3v3 rate predicts team playoff OT hazard (expected near zero).

interactions.mechanism: Games in a series share goalies and defensive systems, so tie indicators across games are positively dependent and the count of OT games has a fatter tail than binomial with the same mean.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare observed counts of OT games per series with binomial(n, p) predictions and estimate beta-binomial rho.

interactions.mechanism: When both teams are within reach of the playoff line a tied game late may be played for the guaranteed point, lowering shot attempts and delaying pulls; the effect should vanish when a team is eliminated or has clinched.
interactions.how_to_test: Within tied-late states, contrast attempts and pull timing between high-leverage and low-leverage standings situations in the same teams.

nonlinearities.shape: Bell-shaped in expected goal gap, decreasing convex in expected total
nonlinearities.why: Tie probability is maximal when gap is zero and falls off with squared gap while higher totals spread mass across more cells; a linear feature in the spread or total mis-orders games near the extremes.

nonlinearities.shape: Threshold below about 3:00 left, then steep increase
nonlinearities.why: Pull probability is near zero until the final minutes and then jumps toward one; time-linear or period-level averages hide that tie conversion happens almost entirely in a short window.

nonlinearities.shape: Convex at low totals
nonlinearities.why: At totals below five goals the 0-0, 1-1 and 2-2 cells dominate and small changes in dispersion move tie mass more than at higher totals.

contract.settlement_definition: KXNHLGAME pays YES if the named team wins the single listed NHL game on the official final result, which in the regular season includes overtime and shootout; KXNHLSPREAD pays YES if the named team wins by more than the floor_strike (for example over 2.5 goals, i.e. a margin of three or more) in that game. Ties do not exist in the NHL, so there is no push. Games postponed but started within 48h stay open; cancelled or unstarted-in-48h games resolve to a fair price. KXNHLPRES, KXNHLSERIES and KXNHLMVP are filed under this archetype in the ledger but are season/series/award contracts.

rules_evidence.quote: If Vancouver wins the New York R vs Vancouver NHL game originally scheduled for Nov 13, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: The winner contract is plain 'wins the game' with no regulation-only qualifier, so OT and shootout wins count as wins; the text never mentions shootouts explicitly.

rules_evidence.quote: If New York R wins by over 2.5 goals in the New York R vs Edmonton NHL game originally scheduled for Nov 9, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: Spread rungs are 'wins by over x.5' (strike_type greater, floor_strike 2.5) so the YES event is a final margin of at least 3; there is no explicit regulation-only or empty-net exclusion.

rules_evidence.quote: 1) Regulation wins 2) Regulation and overtime wins 3) Total wins 4) Head-to-head points
rules_evidence.establishes: Presidents' Trophy ties are broken by regulation wins first, so a points-race contract must track regulation vs overtime wins; this contract is a season future filed in the wrong archetype.

variants_and_edge_cases: Shootout games: the NHL box score awards the shootout winner a one-goal margin, so a shootout win can never contribute to a spread rung of 1.5 or higher; KXNHLSPREAD text does not state this, so the official-score reading is an inference.

Strike ladder: KXNHLSPREAD rungs are one-sided 'wins by over x' contracts per team (1.5, 2.5, ...), so the underdog 'wins by over 2.5' contract and the favourite's are separate markets with very different tail probabilities.
Empty-net goals count toward the final margin: a one-goal late lead turns into a two-goal margin on an empty net, which matters for the 1.5 rung and for 2.5 via two-goal leads.

KXNHLPRES, KXNHLSERIES and KXNHLMVP are long-horizon contracts whose mechanism (points race, series bracket, voter model) is handled under the futures and awards archetypes; KXNHLSERIES and KXNHLMVP have no listed markets and no rules text.

mechanism.summary: Win and margin contracts are functionals of the final goal-difference distribution. Each team's regulation goals are an overdispersed count with mean set by shot volume, shot quality and the opposing goalie; the difference has a near-symmetric bell shape centred on the rating gap plus home ice. The winner contract then adds a resolution rule for regulation ties: overtime and a shootout decide the point with something close to a coin flip, so full-game win probability is a compressed version of regulation win probability. Spread rungs of 1.5 and 2.5 are tail masses of the same distribution, shaped by empty-net goals that convert one-goal leads into two-goal margins and by score effects that make leaders defend. Information arrives mostly as goalie and lineup confirmations in the hours before puck drop, so the main source of mispricing is the speed and size of translating lineup news into expected goal difference, not the base rating.

stages.name: Team strength to expected goal difference
stages.description: Each team's rating is built from score-adjusted 5v5 xG share, special-teams xG and goaltending, then combined into an expected regulation goal difference for this pairing with a home-ice constant. Early in the season (now is early November, roughly a dozen games in) current-season xG is a noisy estimate and must be blended with a preseason prior built from last year's rating, roster turnover and age; the blend weight on current data grows with games played. Opponent adjustment and score-effects correction matter because leading teams are outshot.
stages.distribution: Latent team ratings with posterior uncertainty (sd of order 0.15-0.25 goals per game early in the year); realised goal difference per game has sd near 2.3 goals.

stages.name: Goalie and lineup confirmation shocks
stages.description: Starting goalies are confirmed 1-3 hours before puck drop; replacing a strong starter with a backup moves the opponent's expected goals by a few tenths per game, and a missing top skater or defence pair moves the team's own rate. The size of the shock depends on who the replacement is and on how many minutes shift, so status alone (out/in) is not enough; a value-over-replacement estimate per player turns news into a goal-difference delta. Second games of back-to-backs raise backup probability and add travel fatigue.
stages.distribution: Discrete scenario mixture (starter A or B per team) with continuous skater-impact adjustment; confirmation timing is stochastic and information-vintage sensitive.

stages.name: Margin shaping: score effects and empty-net goals
stages.description: Final margin is not the 60-minute margin of a stationary process: teams with the lead shoot less, and after the trailing goalie is pulled empty-net goals add to the leader's margin. A one-goal lead at 3:00 left converts to a margin of two or more with large probability, so tails at 1.5 and 2.5 are fatter than a pure Skellam of full-game rates implies. The pull time and 6v5 success rate differ by team and coach.
stages.distribution: Skellam core with a late-game jump component; empty-net goals add +1 to the leader's margin with probability of roughly 40-60 percent when a one-goal lead holds past 3:00.

stages.name: Regulation ties, overtime and shootout resolution
stages.description: About a quarter of regular-season games are level after 60 minutes; the winner contract then depends on a five-minute 3v3 period and a shootout. 3v3 overtime is high-event and star-driven, and shootout is near a coin flip with small shooter and goalie effects, so conditional on a tie the win probability sits within a few points of 50 percent with a small home edge. The settlement mapping also matters: a decided shootout is a one-goal margin and goals scored in OT count as ordinary goals for margin.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli resolution with p near 0.5 conditional on tie (a few points of rating-driven tilt); overtime adds a one-goal-margin atom, never two or more.

pace_volume.note: Pace sets how many goals occur but the win and margin contracts depend on the difference between teams rather than the total; pace enters only through dispersion of the difference, already in total_goal_dispersion.

officiating_rules.note: Referee crews shift penalty counts for both teams symmetrically and their effect on the goal difference is second-order relative to goalie and lineup swings; the OT format rule is handled under settlement.

nhl.settlement_goal_pmf.label: Settlement-adjusted final-margin distribution (regulation, OT, shootout, empty net)
nhl.settlement_goal_pmf.mechanism: Maps team goal-rate parameters to the full pmf of final margin under official scoring rules.
nhl.settlement_goal_pmf.rationale: Moneyline, spread and regulation-winner contracts read different functionals of one distribution; building each from its own ad hoc model creates inconsistent prices. The pmf must apply: regulation bivariate counts, late empty-net transitions, an OT goal as a one-goal margin, and a shootout as a one-goal margin with a near-even winner.
nhl.settlement_goal_pmf.measurement: Simulate or enumerate: regulation (H, A) from fitted bivariate overdispersed counts at 55:00 plus a final-5-minute jump process using team pull-time and 6v5 rates; if tied at 60:00 draw OT with 3v3 goal hazard (regular season) giving +/-1 margin, else shootout winner with p = 0.5 + shrunk team SO talent (k=60 attempts) giving +/-1. Output P(margin >= m) for m=1..6 per team and P(regulation tie). Validate by reproducing the league margin histogram (about 25 percent one-goal games) per season.
raw_data: final and regulation scores, OT/SO flags, goal times, strength situationCode
nhl.settlement_goal_pmf.why: Single source of truth for KXNHLGAME and KXNHLSPREAD rungs so that win and spread prices are mutually consistent.

nhl.lineup_impact_delta.label: Lineup impact delta from player value model (skater and goalie)
nhl.lineup_impact_delta.mechanism: Converts who is in or out into a change in expected goal difference using per-player impact estimates.
nhl.lineup_impact_delta.rationale: Injury status flags tell who is missing but not what it costs; a top-pair defenceman, a first-line centre and a starting goalie have different values, and replacements play different minutes. The cost must be computed from minutes redistributed times impact difference.
nhl.lineup_impact_delta.measurement: Estimate per-skater impact as regularised adjusted xG per 60 at 5v5 (ridge RAPM on shift-level data, 3-season window, half-life 1.5 seasons, shrink toward position mean) plus special-teams impact per PP/PK minute; for the projected lineup compute delta = sum_over_players(proj_TOI_new x impact_new) minus same for base lineup, restated as goals per 60 and then x 60/60 per game; for goalies use shrunk GSAx per 1000 shots (k=2000 shots) scaled by opponent shot volume. As-of rule: use lineups published by the team at the time of prediction; keep prior vintages.
raw_data: shift-level data: player, start/end, strength, score; projected lineups; player ratings by season
nhl.lineup_impact_delta.why: Turns the existing injury status flags into a goal-difference number so a late scratch is priced in goals rather than binary news.

nhl.prior_to_current_blend.label: Preseason prior blend weight by games played
nhl.prior_to_current_blend.mechanism: Weights current-season data against a preseason prior as a function of sample size.
nhl.prior_to_current_blend.rationale: At this point in the season (early November) a team has played about 12-15 games; xG share has a stabilisation point of several dozen games, so raw current xG overstates differences and ignores roster turnover.
nhl.prior_to_current_blend.measurement: Prior = last two seasons' score-adjusted rating (weights 0.6/0.4) adjusted by net roster change (minutes-weighted impact of arrivals minus departures) and age curve; posterior = (n x current + k x prior)/(n + k) with k in the 25-40 games range fit by minimising out-of-sample log loss of game result; recompute weekly. Report posterior sd to the simulator.
free_sources: Own computation from MoneyPuck/Natural Stat Trick history
raw_data: team-game xG for/against by season

nhl.prior_to_current_blend.why: Early-season ratings are the biggest source of rating error in an otherwise efficient market; the blend sets how much current xG should count.

nhl.xg_for.reason: Offence component of team strength; should be score-adjusted and combined with xg_against into a net rate and pace rather than used as two independent features.

nhl.xg_against.reason: Defence component; highly collinear with xg_for through shared pace and score effects, so it is the matchup pair that carries the signal.

nhl.goalie_start.reason: Confirmed starter is the largest scheduled shock to expected goals against; the price must be a mixture before confirmation.

nhl.goalie_quality.reason: Needed, but GSAx is a low-persistence statistic so it must be shrunk heavily (thousands of shots) or it injects noise.

nhl.special_teams.reason: Net PP/PK xG matters at the margin; the bulk effect depends on penalty counts, which are noisy per game.

nhl.injuries_pit.reason: Needs the point-in-time vintage but is only a status flag; value comes only after conversion to goals with a player impact model.

nhl.rest_travel.reason: Largely acts through backup-goalie probability on back-to-backs; keep as a conditional on starter identity, not as an independent edge.

nhl.venue.reason: Home ice is a small constant; the 'shot counting bias' in the label affects shot-based features, not the result, so it belongs to feature construction not prediction.

nhl.pdo_regression.reason: Valid shrinkage for results-based ratings, but largely subsumed once ratings are xG-based plus a goalie term.

nhl.reg_tie_model.reason: Gives P(regulation tie) which compresses full-game win probability toward 50 percent and decides the regulation-vs-OT split needed by settlement.

nhl.ot_so.reason: Determines who wins a regulation tie; near a coin flip so its marginal value is a few points of probability at most.

nhl.empty_net.reason: Directly controls the margin tails at 1.5 and 2.5; mislabelled secondary in the draft.

nhl.total_goal_dispersion.reason: Sets variance of goal difference; matters for rung probabilities more than for moneyline.

nhl.standings_stakes.reason: Relevant mainly in late-season games with rest or resting stars; negligible in November.

m.quote_history.reason: Kalshi's own price path is the object being compared with the model; using it as a predictor is circular, it is only for measuring reaction speed.

m.external_lines.reason: Sportsbook prices are a benchmark, not a causal input; mislabelled secondary in the draft and would contaminate a fundamentals-only model.

m.rules_text.reason: Fixes that OT and shootout wins count and defines spread strike construction.

interactions.mechanism: Goals saved above a replacement goalie scale with how many dangerous shots the opponent produces, so a backup start costs a high-volume attacking opponent more than a low-volume one; effect is proportional, not additive.
interactions.how_to_test: Interact goalie quality delta with opponent xG-for per 60 in a goal-difference regression and test the product term.

interactions.mechanism: A one-goal lead past about three minutes triggers a pull and then a high chance of a two-goal margin; spread rungs at 1.5 and 2.5 respond to the leader's EN success and to the trailer's pull time, which are team specific.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare realised P(margin >= 2 | lead by 1 at 3:00) across teams grouped by 6v5 profile.

interactions.mechanism: Full-game win probability equals regulation win probability plus tie probability times roughly one half; the compression is stronger the higher the tie rate, so for a heavy favourite the OT/SO path cuts the favourite's moneyline by more than the same rating gap implies in regulation.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress realised win on regulation-win model probability and tie probability; test coefficient on the tie term against 0.5 times its value.

interactions.mechanism: A rest disadvantage matters mainly if the tired team starts its backup; when the starter plays anyway the residual penalty is small, so the rest flag should be conditioned on confirmed starter.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate the back-to-back coefficient separately for games with starter vs backup in net.

interactions.mechanism: Weight on current-season xG rises with games played and saturates once a few dozen games are in; before that the posterior is dominated by the prior so large xG gaps early in the year should be discounted.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit blend weight against games played and test log-loss improvement versus a constant weight in October-November games.

interactions.mechanism: Late in the season teams with clinched seeds rest stars; the impact delta of a healthy scratch is valued the same as an injury only if rest is not strategic, so stakes decide whether an absence is persistent news or a one-night event.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare model residuals for games with unannounced rest absences across stakes terciles after April 1.

nonlinearities.shape: Concave in shots faced; heavily shrunk
nonlinearities.why: The information in goals-saved-above-expected grows with shots faced but with diminishing returns, and early-season GSAx has near-zero predictive weight so the effective coefficient is a concave function of sample size.

nonlinearities.shape: Step in lead size and time remaining
nonlinearities.why: Empty-net goal probability is near zero except for one-goal leads inside the last few minutes, then jumps; models that average over game time understate the 2.5 rung.

nonlinearities.shape: Tails fatten with expected total
nonlinearities.why: Higher total environments widen the goal-difference distribution, so the same expected gap implies higher probability of a three-goal margin; spread rung probabilities are convex in total.

contract.settlement_definition: KXNHLTOTAL pays YES if the two teams collectively score more than the floor_strike (for example 11.5) goals in the listed game; goals in regulation and overtime count normally and a shootout is recorded as one goal awarded to the winner, so a shootout game adds exactly one to the total. KXNHLTEAMTOTAL pays YES if the named team scores over its floor_strike (for example 5.5) with the same overtime inclusion and the shootout winner credited one additional goal. Postponed games remain open if started within 48h, else fair-price resolution. KXNHLSERIESTOTALGOAL has no listed markets or rules text.

rules_evidence.quote: If the game is decided by a shootout, the shootout result will be recorded as one goal awarded to the winning team.
rules_evidence.establishes: Total goals in a shootout game equal regulation tied score times two plus one, so odd totals gain mass; the target is not pure hockey goals.

rules_evidence.quote: Team totals include goals scored in overtime. If the game goes to a shootout, the shootout winner is credited with one additional goal
rules_evidence.establishes: A team total counts OT goals and a shootout winner gets +1, which lifts the team total of a winner of a tied game and makes it asymmetric between teams.

rules_evidence.quote: Goals scored during regulation and overtime count as normal.
rules_evidence.establishes: Empty-net goals and OT goals count as ordinary goals; the listed strike 11.5 shows ladders extend deep into the tail.

variants_and_edge_cases: Shootout credit: when the score is level after OT the game total is 2k+1 and the winner's team total is k+1; in the regular season about a tenth of games go to a shootout, so this +1 is not negligible for half-goal rungs at 5.5 or 6.5.
Playoffs have no shootout, so the +1 credit never applies and totals are pure regulation plus continuous OT goals; the model must switch rule set by season type.
Ladder tails: strikes like 11.5 and team-total 5.5 are far-tail events whose probability is set by dispersion and meltdown mixtures rather than by the mean.
KXNHLSERIESTOTALGOAL (series total goals) has no markets listed and its aggregation window and shootout treatment are unknown.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official NHL game summary (goals by period including OT, shootout winner); Kalshi settles by the league record plus the stated shootout convention.

mechanism.summary: Total goals are the sum of two overdispersed counts, each equal to shot volume times shot quality times the opposing goalie's conversion, plus power-play goals that depend on how many penalties are called, and a late-game component of empty-net goals. The pair of teams matters multiplicatively, not additively: pace of a game is the product of both teams' tempo preferences and the defensive suppression each applies. After regulation, overtime goals add to the total and a shootout adds a fixed one-goal credit, which moves mass onto odd totals in tied games, a settlement feature that raw hockey goal models omit. Team totals are the single-team marginals, dominated by the opposing goalie, the team's own power-play share and the possibility of a goalie meltdown cascade that pushes counts into the tail. High-strike rungs (9.5, 11.5, team 5.5) are priced from the tail of a mixture, which the mean does not determine.

stages.name: Joint shot-attempt volume of the pair
stages.description: Combined attempt volume comes from each team's offensive tempo and the other team's suppression and is shaped by score effects: trailing teams generate more attempts, leaders fewer. The pair composite is log-additive (offence of A plus defence of B plus home term), so a high-pace team against a defensive structure does not simply add the two paces. Volume also varies with penalties because power plays are higher-volume per minute, and with back-to-back fatigue.
stages.distribution: Poisson-gamma counts of attempts per team with a pair-level shared random effect; combined attempts sd of order 8-10 per game with positive team correlation.

stages.name: Chance quality and goalie conversion
stages.description: Each attempt becomes a goal with probability set by location and type (xG), the shooter's finishing and the opposing goalie. Starter identity moves a team's expected goals against by a few tenths per game, and goalie skill is the hardest rate to measure because it takes thousands of shots to separate. Rebounds and danger-zone share make conversion state dependent on shot mix, not just totals.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli per shot with small probability; goals per team approximately Poisson-gamma with mean 2.8-3.2 league-wide and heterogeneity across goalies.

stages.name: Penalties and power-play goal production
stages.description: Special-teams goals are a large and volatile component: the number of minor penalties depends on both teams' styles and the referee pair, each power play converts at roughly a fifth to a quarter of the time, and a minor penalty ends when the power-play team scores, so expected goals per PP minute is concave in PP time. Unit allocation (PP1 vs PP2) changes conversion within a power play. Totals are therefore sensitive to penalty counts, which are high-variance.
stages.distribution: Compound count: Poisson number of power plays times conversion Bernoulli that terminates the penalty; heavy right tail from multi-penalty games.

stages.name: Late game, overtime and shootout mapping to the contract
stages.description: Empty-net goals add a point to the leader's total in close games, regulation ties add an OT period in which goals count, and a shootout adds one credited goal. The mapping therefore transforms the regulation distribution: P(total odd) rises in the regular season relative to the playoffs, and the mass at k+k+1 grows with P(tie). In the playoffs there is no shootout, so the model must branch on season type. Goalie meltdowns (a starter pulled after several goals) create a high-total tail through a weaker relief goalie.
stages.distribution: Mixture: regulation count plus Bernoulli OT/SO additions; tail mixture component for meltdown games with total above nine.

coaching_scheme.note: No input captures coach-level tempo and risk policy for totals (trap vs forecheck systems, line matching to protect leads); the proxy through pace and score effects only partially reflects it.

nhl.settlement_goal_pmf.label: Settlement-adjusted final-margin distribution (regulation, OT, shootout, empty net)
nhl.settlement_goal_pmf.mechanism: Maps team goal-rate parameters to the full pmf of final margin under official scoring rules.
nhl.settlement_goal_pmf.rationale: Moneyline, spread and regulation-winner contracts read different functionals of one distribution; building each from its own ad hoc model creates inconsistent prices. The pmf must apply: regulation bivariate counts, late empty-net transitions, an OT goal as a one-goal margin, and a shootout as a one-goal margin with a near-even winner.
nhl.settlement_goal_pmf.measurement: Simulate or enumerate: regulation (H, A) from fitted bivariate overdispersed counts at 55:00 plus a final-5-minute jump process using team pull-time and 6v5 rates; if tied at 60:00 draw OT with 3v3 goal hazard (regular season) giving +/-1 margin, else shootout winner with p = 0.5 + shrunk team SO talent (k=60 attempts) giving +/-1. Output P(margin >= m) for m=1..6 per team and P(regulation tie). Validate by reproducing the league margin histogram (about 25 percent one-goal games) per season.
raw_data: final and regulation scores, OT/SO flags, goal times, strength situationCode
nhl.settlement_goal_pmf.why: Totals and team totals read the same pmf with different functionals; the shootout +1 credit and empty-net goals change odd-total mass, which a goals-only model does not reproduce.

nhl.pp_termination_unit_split.label: Power-play termination and unit-time split
nhl.pp_termination_unit_split.mechanism: Expected PP goals per penalty given that a minor ends on a goal and PP1/PP2 share the clock.
nhl.pp_termination_unit_split.rationale: PP time is not additive: a two-minute minor ends when the power-play team scores, so goals per PP are concave in minutes, and the first unit plays roughly the first 60-80 seconds, so PP1 production dominates short power plays. Using PP time x rate overstates multi-goal PP games and misallocates credit among players.
nhl.pp_termination_unit_split.measurement: From play-by-play, for each team and season compute: (a) conversion per PP opportunity (minor penalties only, excluding coincident and 4v4 states), (b) hazard of a PP goal as a function of elapsed PP seconds in 15-second bins, (c) PP1 share of PP time as a function of elapsed seconds, (d) PP goal share by unit. Shrink team hazard to league with k=150 PP opportunities and 2-season half-life. Expected PP goals = sum over expected penalties of integral hazard x survival; keep major and double-minor cases separate.
free_sources: NHL API play-by-play with penalty events and situationCode
raw_data: penalty events (type, minutes), PP start/end, goals with strength state, shift data for unit membership
nhl.pp_termination_unit_split.why: Gives the power-play part of totals as a compound count with termination rather than a product of time and rate, which fattens the penalty-heavy tail of the over rungs.

nhl.pair_attempt_volume.label: Pair attempt-volume composite (log-additive team tempo model)
nhl.pair_attempt_volume.mechanism: Expected combined attempts from offence-for and defence-against terms fit jointly.
nhl.pair_attempt_volume.rationale: Combined pace is not the average of the two teams' season paces: each team's attempts depend on its own offence and the opponent's suppression and on score effects, and the two teams' counts are correlated through game state. A pair composite avoids double counting.
nhl.pair_attempt_volume.measurement: Fit a Poisson regression of 5v5 attempts per 60 for each team-game: log E = mu + off_team + def_opp + home + score-state adjustment, with ridge penalty and 2-season half-life; game attempts = sum of both teams' predictions x projected 5v5 minutes (60 minus expected PP/PK minutes). Add pair random effect with variance estimated from residual covariance. Evaluate pace-weighted xG, not raw attempts, when converting to goals.
free_sources: Natural Stat Trick attempts by team-game
raw_data: team-game attempts, minutes by strength, score state
nhl.pair_attempt_volume.why: Replaces the single combined pace number with a matchup-specific attempt forecast for the pair, where combined-pace errors are a first-order driver of totals.

nhl.pace.reason: Volume driver of totals, but a single combined number is too crude; should be replaced by the pair composite so offence and suppression enter log-additively.

nhl.xg_for.reason: Converts volume to expected goals through chance quality; must be strength-split and score adjusted to avoid leader/trailer bias.

nhl.xg_against.reason: Opponent suppression quality; the lineup-specific value matters more than the season average, which the draft notes correctly.

nhl.shots_against.reason: SOG against with quality is just the defensive half of xG already carried by xg_against and the pair attempt composite; carrying it separately double counts suppression.

nhl.goalie_start.reason: Confirmed starter shifts expected goals against by tenths; for team totals this is the single largest pre-puck-drop change.

nhl.goalie_quality.reason: Needed for conversion; shrunk GSAx is the right form but persistence is weak so its coefficient is small.

nhl.goalie_danger_split.reason: Danger-split save rates over a season rest on small samples per zone and overfit; the information beyond overall shrunk GSAx is slight for a totals prediction.

nhl.special_teams.reason: Efficiency of PP/PK units is persistent only modestly; useful after mapping to penalty counts with termination effects.

nhl.penalty_rates.reason: Penalty counts drive a high-variance goal component; per-team taken and drawn rates are persistent enough to use after shrinkage.

nhl.officials.reason: The penalty_rates label already includes referee crew tendencies, so officials is the same effect named twice; the crew term should be one additive term in a penalty model.

nhl.empty_net.reason: Empty-net goals count toward totals and have a team-specific pull policy; mislabelled secondary because it adds a point in close games.

nhl.rest_travel.reason: Mostly acts via backup goalie probability and fatigue; keep conditional on starter identity.

nhl.injuries_pit.reason: Needs lineup vintage; absences change both PP units and 5v5 quality, but status must be converted to goals.

nhl.pdo_regression.reason: Regresses recent goal luck; useful for early-season ratings that are results-based but redundant when ratings are xG based.

nhl.total_goal_dispersion.reason: Rung probabilities in the tails depend on dispersion and covariance rather than on means.

nhl.venue.reason: Rinks differ in scoring factor and in shot recording; useful as a small additive term, not as a major driver.

m.ladder_structure.reason: Cross-rung monotonicity and implied distributions of Kalshi prices are diagnostics for stale quotes, not causes of goals.

m.rules_text.reason: The shootout +1 credit and the inclusion of OT goals are stated only in the rules text and change the target variable itself.

nhl.opp_supp.reason: Position-level opponent suppression is an individual-skater input; for a game total it is subsumed by team xG against and adds only noise.

nhl.shot_location.reason: Location mix is the ingredient of xG; entering it beside xG double counts the same information.

interactions.mechanism: Expected goals equal attempts times conversion, so an extra 5 attempts matter more against a weak goalie than a strong one; additive pace and quality effects misprice games where fast teams face elite goalies and slow teams face weak ones.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress game goals on log attempts, log quality and their product, and compare with an additive specification by out-of-sample deviance.

interactions.mechanism: Goals per power play flatten with penalty minutes because a minor ends on a goal, and PP1 does most of the work early, so doubling expected penalties adds less than double the PP goals; the effect is larger for strong PP units that score early.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate PP goal hazard by elapsed PP seconds and compare predicted goals under time x rate versus the hazard-with-termination model.

interactions.mechanism: The shootout credit of +1 applies only in regular-season games tied after 65 minutes, so it adds mass to odd totals in proportion to P(tie) and to nothing in the playoffs; half-goal rungs at 5.5 and 6.5 therefore have a season-type-specific probability shift.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare realised over frequency on 5.5 and 6.5 rungs for regular season vs playoffs against a rule-free model and measure the residual.

interactions.mechanism: When a starter is pulled after several goals, the relief goalie's save rate is lower and the trailing team presses, switching the game into a high-total regime; the right tail of the ladder (9.5 to 11.5) is driven by this regime, not by a larger mean.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit a two-component mixture to total goals with a meltdown indicator and test tail calibration for totals of nine or more.

interactions.mechanism: Empty-net goals appear only when a one-goal game is still live late; the number of such goals interacts with the team pull policy, and rink effects on shot recording are negligible compared with this late-game jump.
interactions.how_to_test: Count EN goals per game by closeness at 3:00 left and compare against totals across rungs 5.5 to 7.5.

nonlinearities.shape: Concave in expected penalty minutes
nonlinearities.why: Because a minor penalty ends on a goal and a second unit takes over, expected PP goals grow less than linearly in penalty minutes, so linear penalty features overstate high-penalty games.

nonlinearities.shape: Convex tails above 8 goals
nonlinearities.why: Probability of 9 or more total goals is driven by dispersion and mixture components; a small increase in dispersion raises the far tail multiplicatively while barely changing 5.5 rungs.

nonlinearities.shape: Weak slope with heavy shrinkage
nonlinearities.why: Observed GSAx has little persistence, so the effective effect on goals against is a flat, noisy slope that only becomes steep for goalies with several thousand shots of evidence.

contract.settlement_definition: KXNHLSAVE pays YES if the named goaltender records at least the stated number of saves (threshold 25+, floor_strike 24.5) in the listed NHL game. If the goalie is active but never enters the game the market settles to the last fair market price before game start, so a backup who dresses and does not play is a void-like fair-price outcome rather than NO; once he enters, the market settles on saves recorded. Whether overtime saves and shootout shots count, and what happens if the goalie is not on the active roster at all, is not stated in the sampled text.

rules_evidence.quote: If a player is active but never enters the game, the market settles to the last fair market price before game start.
rules_evidence.establishes: A dressed goalie who does not play is settled at the last traded fair price, so the effective distribution is conditional on entering, with a fair-price component that removes starter-uncertainty risk.

rules_evidence.quote: Once a player enters the game, the market settles based on the player's saves recorded.
rules_evidence.establishes: Settlement counts the player's own recorded saves, so a mid-game pull or relief appearance truncates exposure and the relief goalie's partial game would count only his own saves.

variants_and_edge_cases: Pulled goalie: a starter replaced after four goals keeps the saves already recorded, so the lower tail below the rung is bimodal (full game vs early pull), and the backup who relieves has a separate small exposure.

Overtime: saves in the 5-minute 3v3 period are official goalie saves and plausibly count toward 'in the game', but the text does not say; shootout shots are not counted in official saves, an assumption the text does not confirm.
Active-but-never-enters versus scratched or not dressed: the text covers 'active' players only, so a goalie who is not on the game roster is a CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS case (void, fair price or NO).
Strike construction is a single 25+ style contract per rung; rung ladder for a goalie is nested and monotone in the threshold, and the sampled strike is a one-sided 'at least' contract.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official NHL box score goalie line (saves), as recorded by league scorers; fair-price rule determined by Kalshi.

mechanism.summary: Saves equal shots on goal faced minus goals allowed, so the count is determined first by exposure (how many minutes the named goalie is in net, including the chance he is pulled or never plays), then by the shot flow the opponent produces against this defence, and last by a binomial thinning in which each shot becomes a goal with probability of about one in ten. Volume dominates: the standard deviation of shots faced is several times larger than the effect of goalie skill, and the 25-save rung sits near the median for a typical starter so the probability is steep in the mean. Score effects redistribute shots by minute: trailing teams shoot more, and a goalie on a trailing team faces 6v5 shots late; power plays concentrate shots. Settlement adds a regime: a dressed goalie who never enters pays at fair price, and a pull truncates the total.

stages.name: Exposure: who plays and for how many minutes
stages.description: The named goalie's saves accrue only while he is in net. Exposure is a mixture over start/no-start (a backup who dresses and does not play settles at the last fair price), full 60 minutes versus pulled after a goal burst, and overtime minutes. Back-to-back and recent workload determine start probability, morning-skate signals and team patterns refine it, and confirmation arrives close to puck drop. After a pull, the relief goalie has only a small partial exposure.
stages.distribution: Three-component mixture on minutes: ~0 (no entry, fair-price), partial (pulled at time T, usually after 3-4 goals), and full 60 (+ OT); pull probability roughly one start in ten.

stages.name: Opponent shot flow against this defence
stages.description: Shots on goal faced come from the opponent's attempt volume, the fraction that are on goal rather than blocked or missed, and this defence's suppression, shaped by score state and penalties: power plays generate roughly twice the shot rate of 5v5 and trailing teams shoot more. Opponent SOG-for per 60 by state and defence SOG-against by state combine log-additively; league-average is about 30 shots per game. Overtime adds a short 3v3 high-event period.
stages.distribution: Negative-binomial counts of shots faced with mean near 28-31 and sd about 5-6 (overdispersed relative to Poisson because of PP and score-state clustering).

stages.name: Conversion: goals allowed thin the shot count
stages.description: Each shot becomes a goal with probability set by shot danger and the goalie's skill, so saves given shots are binomial with success probability near 0.9. A goalie of persistent skill moves this by a point or two; shot quality of the opponent mix (rebounds, rush chances) moves it similarly. Goals also change the game: more goals against shift the score state and raise pull risk, so saves and shots are negatively linked at the extremes.
stages.distribution: Binomial thinning of shots with p about 0.90; goals allowed approximately Poisson with mean 2.7-3.0; saves = shots minus goals.

stages.name: Official counting and settlement
stages.description: The recorded save count comes from the league scorer's shot-on-goal decisions, so rink-level recording differences enter directly, and from the treatment of OT and shootout shots, which official statistics handle differently. Because the contract is a threshold on a discrete count, the probability is the upper tail of the saves distribution at 25; ladders for the same goalie are nested rungs.
stages.distribution: Discrete count with threshold at k; probability steep in the mean (a one-save mean shift moves P(25+) by about 8-10 points).

coaching_scheme.note: No input captures the coach's decision rule for pulling a goalie after goals allowed or for scheduling starts (e.g. split starts, rest after a bad outing), which drives both exposure and the truncated lower tail.

nhl.opp_sog_for_rate.label: Opponent shots-on-goal-for rate by strength state, score adjusted
nhl.opp_sog_for_rate.mechanism: Opponent's own shot-on-goal generation per 60 at EV and on the power play.
nhl.opp_sog_for_rate.rationale: The draft carries opponent xG (a quality measure) and the defence's suppression, but saves count shots on goal, so the opponent's volume of on-target shots, separate from danger, is the first-order driver. xG weights shots by quality and understates the effect of low-danger volume teams.
nhl.opp_sog_for_rate.measurement: Per team compute SOG for per 60 at 5v5 (score-and-venue adjusted via regression of SOG rate on score differential bins) and at 5v4, with 2-season half-life 40 games and shrink to league with k=15 games; project game SOG faced = EV_rate_opp x defence_adjustment x projected EV minutes + PP_rate_opp x projected PP minutes. Use log-additive combination with opponent defence SOG-against: log E = mu + off_opp + def_team.
free_sources: Natural Stat Trick team SOG splits
raw_data: team-game SOG by strength state and score state
nhl.opp_sog_for_rate.why: Directly forecasts the number of shots the goalie will see, which is the main variance driver of saves.

nhl.goalie_minutes_in_net_dist.label: Goalie minutes-in-net distribution (entry, pull and overtime)
nhl.goalie_minutes_in_net_dist.mechanism: Probability distribution of the named goalie's exposure in minutes and the relief goalie's partial exposure.
nhl.goalie_minutes_in_net_dist.rationale: The settlement rule makes exposure part of the contract: no entry -> fair-price, entry -> own saves only. Exposure is neither 60 nor zero; pulls and relief appearances create a mass at partial minutes. This is a distribution, not a scalar start probability.
nhl.goalie_minutes_in_net_dist.measurement: From box scores since 2015-16 build for each goalie the empirical pmf of minutes, conditional on starting: P(pulled before 40:00), P(pulled in 40-55), P(full + OT). Shrink each goalie's pull rate to team-coach and league rates with k=25 starts; make pull hazard depend on goals allowed in the first period (0, 1, 2, 3+). Combine with P(start | rest, schedule, report) from the forecast to get an overall mixture, and mark the no-start component as fair-price (excluded from the YES/NO distribution).
free_sources: NHL API boxscore (TOI and shots per goalie)
raw_data: goalie-game: starter flag, TOI, shots faced, goals against, relief entry time, pull reason if recorded
nhl.goalie_minutes_in_net_dist.why: Turns 'goalie plays' into the precise exposure distribution that determines the lower tail and the settlement mixture of this contract.

nhl.arena_sog_recording_factor.label: Arena-level SOG recording factor
nhl.arena_sog_recording_factor.mechanism: Home-arena effect on recorded shots on goal after controlling for teams.
nhl.arena_sog_recording_factor.rationale: Official scorers record SOG; arenas can differ systematically, but the size for SOG is smaller and less certain than for hits or giveaways. A measured factor lets the model decide whether venue matters rather than assuming it.
nhl.arena_sog_recording_factor.measurement: Fit a mixed model log(SOG_game) = team offence + team defence + arena effect + season, using all games from 2015-16 on, with arena random effect shrunk with prior sd 0.03; use arena effect only when its posterior mean exceeds 1.5 times its sd. Re-estimate each season, because tracking and scorer changes alter bias.
raw_data: game-level SOG for each team with arena id
nhl.arena_sog_recording_factor.why: Tests the draft's claim that rink counting bias is a primary driver of saves; if the factor is under two percent the input is dropped.

nhl.ot_shot_exposure.label: Overtime shot exposure given regulation tie probability
nhl.ot_shot_exposure.mechanism: Expected extra shots faced in overtime weighted by probability of a tie.
nhl.ot_shot_exposure.rationale: Overtime is a 3v3 period with high shot density that can add several shots to a goalie's count; its expected contribution is P(OT) times shots per OT period, which can push a goalie across a threshold. It enters only if the contract counts OT, which is not stated.
nhl.ot_shot_exposure.measurement: Estimate team-pair P(regulation tie) from the tie model and shots on goal per 3v3 five-minute period from NHL play-by-play 2015-16 on (pooled mean and sd, team adjustments shrunk with k=200 overtime minutes); expected extra saves = P(tie) x shots_per_OT x (1 - OT goal prob); when playoff 5v5 OT applies use hazard-based shots per 20 minutes.
raw_data: OT shot events with strength, team, goalie
nhl.ot_shot_exposure.why: Provides the OT contribution to a threshold that sits near the median where a few shots matter.

nhl.shots_against.reason: Team SOG allowed is the right volume driver from the defence side; it must be combined with the opponent's SOG-for in a log-additive pair model rather than used alone.

nhl.xg_for.reason: Opponent xG measures shot quality not shot count; saves depend on on-target volume, so quality only matters for goals allowed and is replaced by opponent SOG-for.

nhl.pace.reason: Combined attempt pace includes blocked and missed attempts that never become saves; secondary to SOG-specific measures.

nhl.goalie_start.reason: Identifies who is in net; because a non-playing dressed goalie settles at fair price, its main role is exposure and rate for the starter, not eligibility.

nhl.goalie_start_forecast.reason: Useful before confirmation to weight starters, though the contract's fair-price rule limits the risk from a wrong guess.

nhl.goalie_workload.reason: The text describes rest and back-to-back as start-probability drivers, which is exactly the forecast model; recent save pct is noise.

nhl.goalie_pull_risk.reason: Shapes the lower tail and truncation; unobservable pregame so it must be a hazard model by goals-allowed state.

nhl.score_state.reason: Score effects shift shots by minute and are partially predictable from script; it is an in-game state, so pregame only its expectation is usable.

nhl.game_script_prob.reason: Win probability tilts shots against favourites downward, but the effect is modest compared with shot volume noise.

nhl.penalty_rates.reason: Power plays against raise shots faced; counts are high variance so the contribution is on the dispersion and tails.

nhl.officials.reason: Crew penalty tendency is already part of penalty_rates (its label includes referee crews), so a second input double counts the same effect.

nhl.venue.reason: Draft marks it primary but SOG recording bias is smaller than for hits or giveaways; magnitude unverified, so it is a measured secondary term.

nhl.goalie_quality.reason: Moves save% by a point or two; effect on saves is a fraction of one save per game relative to volume noise.

nhl.injuries_pit.reason: Absences on the defending team change shot suppression modestly; the key injury news for this market is goalie news, covered elsewhere.

nhl.stat_dist.reason: Rung probabilities require a negative-binomial shot count with binomial thinning; the discrete count and overdispersion decide tail probabilities at 25.

m.rules_text.reason: The active-never-enters fair-price rule and the settlement on recorded saves define the distribution being priced.

interactions.mechanism: Expected shots faced is the product of the opponent's shot generation and this defence's allowance, with power-play time as an additional multiplier because PP shot rates are about double 5v5; a high-shot opponent facing a leaky penalty-prone defence compounds all three.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit log SOG with offence, defence and penalty-minute terms and test their products against the additive model.

interactions.mechanism: Saves have a different relationship to shots in the full-game and pulled regimes: a pull after four goals truncates the count well below the rung, so the distribution below 25 is a mixture whose weight depends on early goals allowed, and goalie quality moves the pull weight rather than the mean.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare saves distributions conditional on first-period goals against (0 to 3+) and fit the mixture weight against goalie save rate.

interactions.mechanism: Before confirmation the price must be a mixture over the two goalies; if the backup would face the same volume the mean barely changes, but the rate differs by tenths of a save percentage, so the confirmation move is smaller than for goal markets.
interactions.how_to_test: Measure the price jump at confirmation across starter and backup cases and compare with the model mixture.

interactions.mechanism: Overtime adds a block of shots only when regulation is tied, which shifts the mean by about one shot weighted by the tie probability but moves the probability of crossing 25 more when the base mean is near 24; the effect is largest at the median rung.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress realised crossing of the 25-save rung on regulation saves and an OT indicator and compare to the model prediction.

interactions.mechanism: The goalie of a heavy favourite faces fewer shots because leads shift play to the offensive zone, but the effect saturates: beyond a two-goal lead shots against stay low whilst trailing teams add late pulls, so favourites' goalies have less variance and a lower mean.
interactions.how_to_test: Bin by pregame win probability and compare mean and variance of shots against in each bin.

nonlinearities.shape: S-shaped (cumulative) response of P(25+) to the mean
nonlinearities.why: With sd of shots faced of 5-6 the probability of reaching 25 rises from about 20 to 80 percent as the mean moves from 21 to 29, so a small mean error near the rung causes large probability error.

nonlinearities.shape: Bimodal lower-tail mixture of full and pulled games
nonlinearities.why: A pull converts a typical 25-save game into a 12-18 save game; the saves distribution is a mixture, so a unimodal NB underestimates the mass far below the rung and overestimates it near the mean.

nonlinearities.shape: Saturating in lead size
nonlinearities.why: Shot suppression for the goalie on the leading team saturates after a two-goal lead since leaders play defensively but do not reduce further, while a trailing opponent's late 6v5 shots rise sharply near the end.
