contract.settlement_definition: No live NHL parlay or combo series appears in the ledger, so there is no rules text. The blueprint describes a single contract that pays only if every named leg (team result, spread, total, player stat) occurs in the same game or slate; its fair price is the joint probability of all legs. Whether a voided or fair-priced leg (for example a non-playing skater) removes the leg, collapses the combo to a fair price or settles it No is unknown and is the single most important settlement unknown, since a prop leg in an NHL game has a non-trivial chance of being voided at fair price under sibling rules.
variants_and_edge_cases: Leg void handling: sibling prop rules settle an active-but-never-enters player at the last fair price; if a combo inherits this, the contract payoff after a void is a different function of the remaining legs, not simply the product of the others.

Logically related legs: nested ladder rungs (points 2+ inside points 1+), a team win with the opponent's spread, or a team total leg with the game total leg are not independent and some combinations are impossible, so the pricing must respect implications and exclusions.

Same-game versus cross-game combos: legs from different games are independent except for shared news, whereas same-game legs share latent game drivers; the structure of the contract decides which model is needed.

Leg settlement differences: a shootout adds one goal to totals and team totals but affects margins differently, and third-period legs exclude overtime; each leg inherits its own rule, so a combo is only as clean as its worst-defined leg.
contract.settlement_data_source: Per-leg official NHL game and player statistics; combo-level resolution rules unobserved.

mechanism.summary: The fair price of a combo is the probability of an intersection, which equals the product of marginals times a dependence factor that depends on shared latent drivers. In an NHL game those drivers are few and identifiable: the goal intensity of each team (pace and quality), the goalie states (starter identity and a within-game quality shock including pulls), the number of power plays, the lineup state of key skaters, and the score path that decides empty-net goals and minutes compression. Player legs follow from team goals via an allocation of goals and assists to the skaters on ice, so the right architecture is one game-level simulation that draws latent states, generates team goal events, allocates credit to players, and reads all legs from the same draw. Dependence is not constant: it grows in the tails (blowouts), switches sign for some leg pairs (goalie saves versus totals), and mis-specification compounds because errors in each leg multiply. Settlement of voided legs changes the payoff structure.

stages.name: Leg catalogue and logical structure
stages.description: Each leg is a threshold on a game statistic: win, margin, total, a team's total, a skater's goals, assists, points or shots, a goalie's saves. Some legs imply or exclude each other: points of two or more imply points of one, a team's win excludes the opponent's win, and a team total over implies a minimum for the game total. These deterministic relations determine part of the joint probability exactly and must be imposed before any correlation is estimated.
stages.distribution: Deterministic implications and exclusions among discrete legs; no free parameter, only structural constraints.

stages.name: Shared latent game drivers
stages.description: The legs are tied by a small set of latent variables: total goal intensity (pace times shot quality), goal differential driven by team strength and script, goalie quality shocks (including an early pull), and the number of power plays. A positive shock to total intensity lifts goals, assists and totals together, while a goalie shock moves the opposing team's scoring and the goalie's own saves in different directions. Their joint distribution defines the correlation structure of all legs.
stages.distribution: Low-dimensional latent vector with heavy tails: goal intensity lognormal-like, goalie shock mixture (normal game versus pulled), power plays Poisson.

stages.name: Conditional player legs given team goals
stages.description: Given the simulated team goals and strength states, each goal is allocated to skaters on the ice with probabilities set by their shot shares and credit shares, so a skater's goals, assists and points are conditional on the team's goals and on his minutes. This creates the positive correlation between a team's win leg and its star's points leg and between team total and player points, and it respects the maximum of three points per goal. Minutes compression in blowouts adds a negative link between margin and star shot counts.
stages.distribution: Allocation is multinomial per goal; conditional on g team goals, a skater's points are a thinned binomial-like count with credit probability near 0.6-0.8 for top forwards.

stages.name: Lineup scenarios and settlement mapping
stages.description: Lineup states are discrete and correlated across legs: a starter goalie change or a star scratch moves several legs at once, and a non-playing prop leg may be voided. The scenario tree gives joint probabilities of these states at the contract's decision time. Payoff then depends on the settlement map for voided legs, which changes the combo from an intersection into a conditional-intersection contract.
stages.distribution: Discrete scenario tree with 4-12 leaves; payoff map piecewise over leg statuses (win, lose, void).

opponent_matchup.note: Matchups between specific teams and players are properties of each leg's marginal model; the combo adds nothing matchup-specific beyond the shared latent drivers, which are captured by team means in the simulation.

coaching_scheme.note: Coaching effects enter each leg through team rates, lines and minutes, already part of the marginal leg models; a combo contract does not add a separate coaching mechanism beyond what is in its legs.

environment.note: Rink and travel effects act through team means of each leg and are common across legs in the same game, so they affect the marginals but not the dependence structure beyond what team means carry.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Rest and standings stakes affect lineup and strength states that the scenario tree and team means already carry; no combo-specific schedule mechanism exists.

officiating_rules.note: Referee tendencies shift penalty counts which are part of the shared latent drivers; the combo adds no officiating mechanism of its own beyond the leg-level rules.

nhl.goal_credit_allocation_kernel.label: Goal-credit allocation kernel (probability each skater scores or assists on a team goal)
nhl.goal_credit_allocation_kernel.mechanism: Probability that a skater is credited with the goal, primary or secondary assist, conditional on a team goal at a given strength state and lineup.
nhl.goal_credit_allocation_kernel.rationale: A combo mixing team and player legs needs one coherent mechanism linking team goals to individual stats; a kernel based on on-ice shares and credit shares guarantees consistency and the cap of one goal and two assists per team goal.
nhl.goal_credit_allocation_kernel.measurement: For each skater and strength state (EV, PP, EN) compute: P(on ice | team goal) = team goals scored while on ice / team goals in the state, and P(credit type | on ice, goal) from three seasons of goal events (shrunk to position/line priors with k=30 goals); build for the projected lineup a kernel K[skater, role(goal, A1, A2)] with columns summing to 1 for goals, and at most two assists per goal; in simulation draw each goal's state, then allocate credit by K. Recalibrate so that simulated team assists per goal match league and team averages.
free_sources: NHL API play-by-play (goal credits and on-ice skaters)
raw_data: goal events with on-ice skaters, scorer and assists, strength state
nhl.goal_credit_allocation_kernel.why: Forms the bridge between team-goal legs and player-stat legs so that win, total and points legs come from the same simulated goals.

nhl.lineup_scenario_tree.label: Joint lineup scenario tree (goalies and key skaters)
nhl.lineup_scenario_tree.mechanism: Joint probability over starter goalie for each team and the status of the three or four most influential skaters.
nhl.lineup_scenario_tree.rationale: A single leg's availability probability is not enough: several legs move at once on the same news, and the joint probability of states (e.g., backup in net and star out) is not the product of marginal probabilities because of shared causes such as back-to-backs.
nhl.lineup_scenario_tree.measurement: Define for each team K key players (starting goalie plus top-4 skaters by impact) and enumerate states; estimate P(state) from the team's historical patterns: goalie rotation (consecutive-start rules, back-to-back), injury reports and morning skate evidence; assume independence beyond shared schedule factors unless data show otherwise; limit leaves to those with probability above 1 percent and merge the rest; store each state with its decision-time vintage.
raw_data: lineup reports, goalie starts, injury statuses with timestamps
nhl.lineup_scenario_tree.why: Provides the joint discrete shocks across legs; voided legs and shifted marginals happen on these same states.

nhl.copula_tail_dependence.label: Tail dependence between leg pairs (copula parameters by pair type)
nhl.copula_tail_dependence.mechanism: Dependence in the joint upper and lower tails of leg pairs beyond linear correlation.
nhl.copula_tail_dependence.rationale: Hockey legs show stronger dependence in the tails than in the centre: blowout games produce high totals, large margins and many points together. A Gaussian copula with a pooled correlation underprices joint tail events and overprices central ones.
nhl.copula_tail_dependence.measurement: For each pair type (win-total, win-player points, total-player points, goalie saves-total, total-team total) compute from five seasons of game logs the empirical conditional exceedance chi(u) = P(U>u, V>u)/(1-u) at u = 0.7, 0.8, 0.9 using rank transforms with discrete tie handling; fit Gaussian, Student-t and Clayton copulas by maximum likelihood on the pseudo-observations and choose by out-of-sample joint log-likelihood; shrink pair-type parameters with k=400 games.
free_sources: NHL API player-game and team logs
raw_data: game-level outcomes for all legs: result, margin, total, player stats
nhl.copula_tail_dependence.why: Corrects the Gaussian-correlation shortcut that is the main source of error in joint tails.

nhl.parlay_leg_void_payoff_map.label: Parlay leg-void payoff map
nhl.parlay_leg_void_payoff_map.mechanism: Lookup table mapping each combination of leg statuses (win, lose, void-at-fair-price) to the contract payoff under the rules in force.
nhl.parlay_leg_void_payoff_map.rationale: The fair price depends on what happens to the combo when a leg voids: collapse to fair price, drop the leg, or lose. The same probabilities give different prices under different maps, and none is observed in the sampled rules.
nhl.parlay_leg_void_payoff_map.measurement: From the rules text of each combo series build a table payoff(status vector); where text is missing mark the map as unknown and carry multiple candidate maps (drop-leg, fair-price collapse, lose) with prior weights; compute price under each candidate and report the range; version by rules_text vintage so that changes are visible.
raw_data: rules_primary and rules_secondary per combo series with version
nhl.parlay_leg_void_payoff_map.why: Determines what the combo is worth when a leg voids, which can swing price by more than any modelling edge.

nhl.leg_logical_relations.label: Leg logical-relations map (implications, exclusions, shared ladders)
nhl.leg_logical_relations.mechanism: Deterministic implications and exclusions among legs of the same game.
nhl.leg_logical_relations.rationale: Nested rungs and mutually exclusive outcomes fix part of the joint probability exactly: points 2+ implies points 1+, a team win excludes the opponent win, the spread leg implies the win leg. A correlation model that ignores this can assign probability to impossible combinations.
nhl.leg_logical_relations.measurement: Enumerate for each pair of legs the logical relation under the game's settlement rules (including shootout credit, third-period OT exclusion, and nested player ladders) and store as a matrix of {implies, excludes, independent-by-construction, free}; the simulator rejects draws violating relations and the pricing uses P(A and B) = P(A) for implied and 0 for excluded.
raw_data: leg definitions with period, rung, stat and settlement rules
nhl.leg_logical_relations.why: Prevents impossible or double-counted combinations in the combo price.

nhl.joint_outcome_correlation.reason: The right quantity but a pooled pairwise correlation is insufficient: dependence differs by leg pair and by tail, so it needs tail-dependence parameters and structural relations.

nhl.stat_dist.reason: Marginal count shapes are necessary for each leg but are inputs to the leg models; for the combo the dependence structure matters more.

nhl.game_script_prob.reason: The score-path latent drives win, margin, totals and player minutes together; it is the shared factor that a combo model must expose.

nhl.total_goal_dispersion.reason: Sets variance and tail dependence of team and total goals; secondary because it parameterises the latent intensity.

nhl.goalie_start.reason: A goalie change shifts several legs at once, but as a discrete scenario it is better represented in the lineup scenario tree than as a single input.

nhl.injuries_pit.reason: Late scratches change several legs together; the information needs to be turned into joint scenarios rather than treated as a flag.

nhl.xg_for.reason: Team scoring level enters each goal-related leg; it is a leg marginal input and affects the combo only through the team means of the simulation.

nhl.xg_against.reason: Opponent scoring level for totals and win legs; same role as xg_for, mostly a marginal input rather than a dependence input.

nhl.toi.reason: Player volume for player legs; in the combo it matters only via the conditional allocation of team goals and as a link between margin and star minutes.

m.rules_text.reason: Per-leg settlement and the void treatment of legs change the payoff; no combo rules are observed so this is the largest unknown.

m.ladder_structure.reason: Cross-rung consistency of Kalshi leg prices is a quote diagnostic, not a driver of joint outcomes, and cannot be an input.

interactions.mechanism: P(team wins and star records 2+ points) is much larger than the product of marginals because a win by two or more requires goals and the star is credited on a share of them; the uplift is convex in the number of team goals and falls when blowouts compress the star's minutes.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute P(win and points>=2) by team goals bins and compare with the product and with the simulation.

interactions.mechanism: A backup goalie start and a missing star on the same team are positively linked by schedule (back-to-back) and move the team's win, total and player legs together; the joint probability of lineup states is not the product of the marginal probabilities.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate co-occurrence of backup starts and key absences versus independence in 5 seasons of lineup data.

interactions.mechanism: In the blowout regime (margin three or more) the legs on total, margin and star points are strongly dependent, whereas in the centre the dependence is weak; a single correlation parameter underprices the tail combinations that parlays most often bundle.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit conditional exceedance for pairs at u = 0.8 and 0.9 and compare to the central-correlation Gaussian prediction.

interactions.mechanism: The relation between a goalie's saves leg and the game total leg is non-monotone: high pace lifts both, but a weak goalie lifts the total and lowers saves, so the sign of dependence depends on which latent factor drives the game.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress saves on total goals separately within bins of goalie save percentage shock and of opponent shot volume.

interactions.mechanism: The payoff after a void depends on the map; with nested or implied legs a void can make a leg redundant and change which legs are binding, so the effective probability depends jointly on the map and the logical relations.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute combo price under each candidate void map and flag combos for which the maps differ by more than a tick.

interactions.mechanism: Win and star shots legs are negatively linked only in the blowout regime where the leader's stars lose minutes; below a two-goal lead there is no link, so the dependence is a threshold in the lead.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate the correlation between team win margin and star SOG for margins below two versus three or more.

nonlinearities.shape: Tail-dependent, stronger in the upper tail
nonlinearities.why: Combined events such as large win margin with high total with star points occur in a small set of high-scoring games, so joint exceedance probabilities grow faster than a constant correlation implies.

nonlinearities.shape: Piecewise: star minutes fall only at margins above two goals
nonlinearities.why: Compression of stars' minutes appears in blowouts only, creating a kink in the relation between margin and star counts and a negative dependence regime absent in close games.

nonlinearities.shape: Error amplification across legs
nonlinearities.why: Probability errors on each leg multiply in an intersection, so a five percent relative error per leg becomes about 20 percent over four legs; the effect is multiplicative in log-probability, not additive.

contract.settlement_definition: These are long-horizon binary contracts resolved at the end of the 2026-27 season or playoffs: KXNHLPLAYOFF pays YES if the named team qualifies for the playoffs, KXNHLWEST/KXNHLEAST if the team wins its conference final, KXNHL if it wins the Stanley Cup, KXNHLRECORDWORST if it has the worst regular season record (league tie-break procedures then dead-heat 1/N), KXNHLFINALSEXACT the exact Cup final series score, and KXNHLCALDER/NORRIS/VEZINA/HART/ROSS/RICHARD pay if the named player wins the award or stat title, with ties paying $1/N rounded down. Source of truth is the NHL's official standings, bracket results and award announcements.

rules_evidence.quote: If the Washington Capitals qualify for the playoffs in the 2026-27 NHL season, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: Playoff qualifier resolves on qualification under league rules (top three per division plus wild cards), so the tie-break rules and the points cut-off determine the boundary, and no secondary text defines it.

rules_evidence.quote: If the Winnipeg Jets win the 2026-27 NHL Western Conference Finals, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: Conference champion pays on winning the conference final series, a conditional on reaching it, so the contract mixes qualification, seed path and two series.

rules_evidence.quote: official tie-breaking procedures will be applied until a single team remains
rules_evidence.establishes: Worst record ties are broken by league procedures and, if still tied, dead-heat 1/N; the contract is a points-minimum event with tiebreaks that favour regulation-win counts.

rules_evidence.quote: positions will pay $1/N (rounded down to the nearest cent), where N is the number of tied participants
rules_evidence.establishes: Award ties pay 1/N, so a tied award is a partial payout; the award is decided by voters, not by a statistic.

variants_and_edge_cases: Mixed mechanisms in one archetype: team qualification (points race), conference and Cup (bracket simulation), worst record (points minimum with tiebreaks), and six award or stat-title contracts (voter model or counting leader); each needs a different generating process.

Stat-title markets (Art Ross: points leader, Rocket Richard: goals leader) are counting-leader contracts where ties are possible and tiebreak and dead-heat rules matter, whereas Hart, Vezina, Norris and Calder are voted awards with different electorates.

Several series (KXNHL Stanley Cup, KXNHLEAST, KXNHLHART, KXNHLVEZINA, KXNHLRICHARD, KXNHLFINALSEXACT) list no markets and no rules text, so their exact wording (for example voting body or final score format) is unseen.

Time horizon: markets trade for months, so information (injuries, trades at the deadline, goalie form) and price paths matter and a team's death in the race resolves its contracts early only in effect, not by rule.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official NHL standings and playoff bracket results; award announcements by the league; stat leaders from official NHL statistics.

mechanism.summary: A team future is the output of a two-layer simulation with uncertainty in the inputs. Layer one is the unknown team strength: posterior ratings from xG, goaltending and roster, with a drift and an uncertainty that matter as much as the mean because title odds are a convex function of rating. Layer two is the league mechanism: 82 games produce points through wins and overtime or shootout loser points; the playoff boundary is the 16th best record under division-and-wildcard rules with tiebreaks that favour regulation wins; the bracket then fixes opponents and home ice, and best-of-seven series amplify the variance of goaltending and injuries. Awards and stat titles are a separate process: counting leaders through rate times games with injury risk, or voted awards through a model of electorates and narratives. Settlement ties (dead heat, 1/N, tiebreakers) alter probabilities near the boundary. Information arrives slowly but with jumps (injuries, trades), so the posterior update is part of the price.

stages.name: Team strength posterior with drift and uncertainty
stages.description: Each team's strength is a latent rating combining last season's performance, roster changes, age curves, goaltending and current-season xG, with weight on current data growing with games played (early November is about 14 games in). The posterior has an uncertainty of order 0.2 goals per game early in the year and follows a drift because of injuries and trades, so simulating with point ratings would overstate certainty and understate the probability of surprises.
stages.distribution: Gaussian-like posterior with sd 0.15-0.25 goals per game shrinking through the season, plus jump components for injuries and trades.

stages.name: Regular-season points accumulation and loser-point structure
stages.description: Remaining games are simulated with rest, travel, home and opponent strength; each game gives two points to the winner and one to an overtime or shootout loser, so a team's points include a loser-point stream that is partly skill and mostly noise. The points distribution across 82 games has sd about 7-8 points; the playoff cut-off sits near the mid-90s with its own uncertainty, and strength of schedule within division changes the remaining path.
stages.distribution: Sum of 82 game outcomes with 3-point structure (win in regulation 2, OT/SO win 2, OT/SO loss 1); points sd about 7-9; tiebreak counts (regulation wins) are a separate lattice.

stages.name: Qualification boundary, seeding and bracket path
stages.description: The top three teams in each division plus two wild cards per conference qualify; division winners face wild cards, so seeding determines opponent and home ice, and the same strength gives different championship odds by path. Tiebreakers (regulation wins first, then regulation-plus-overtime wins, then head-to-head etc.) decide close races, and a team's Cup probability depends on which seed it ends in and on rivals' seeds.
stages.distribution: Qualification is a threshold on a noisy points total; bracket path is a combinatorial function of the final standings with discrete seeds.

stages.name: Playoff series, goaltending variance and injuries
stages.description: Each series is best-of-seven with 2-2-1-1-1 home ice; the better team's single-game win probability is only 55-65 percent, so series are high variance, and goaltending hot streaks and injuries are large contributors beyond rating. The playoff environment changes penalty rates, depth usage and overtime format, and series state (games played, rest) updates probabilities.
stages.distribution: Series win probability from best-of-seven recursion with single-game p near 0.55-0.62 and extra variance from goalie performance beyond binomial.

stages.name: Awards and stat titles
stages.description: The award contracts resolve by voters or by statistic: Art Ross and Rocket Richard are counting-leader outcomes (points, goals) with games-played tiebreaks, Hart, Norris and Calder are decided by writers, Vezina by general managers. Probabilities come from projected production, team success, voter-preference model (points, goals, wins, narrative), eligibility rules and an injury hazard that can end a campaign. Finalist announcements and ballot dates make step changes in information.
stages.distribution: Leader contracts: sum of games-by-rate with sd of order 8-10 points; voted awards: multinomial-logit over candidates with heavy-tailed vote shares.

coaching_scheme.note: No input captures coach quality or in-season coaching changes as a driver of team strength and playoff performance; coaching change effects on ratings are unquantified and enter only through the news input.

officiating_rules.note: Playoff officiating tendencies (fewer calls, differing power-play counts) are only represented through the playoff context flag; there is no quantified input that translates officiating regime into series win probability.

nhl.rating_posterior_uncertainty.label: Team rating posterior uncertainty and in-season drift
nhl.rating_posterior_uncertainty.mechanism: Posterior standard deviation of each team's strength and its random-walk drift per game.
nhl.rating_posterior_uncertainty.rationale: A season or title simulation using point ratings is overconfident: the spread of true strengths and the error of the estimate both matter, and title probability is convex in rating so uncertainty raises the probability of mid-tier teams. Early-season data are noisy.
nhl.rating_posterior_uncertainty.measurement: Fit a state-space model: rating_t = rating_{t-1} + eta (sd 0.02 goals/game per game, estimated by out-of-sample likelihood), observation = score-adjusted xG differential and goal differential with measurement sd from game-level residuals; initialise with preseason prior (sd 0.25 goals/game). Output posterior mean and sd per team per day; draw ratings from the posterior in each simulation run. Re-estimate drift variance each season.
free_sources: Own computation from MoneyPuck/Natural Stat Trick game data
raw_data: team-game goals, xG, score effects, date; preseason projections
nhl.rating_posterior_uncertainty.why: Controls overconfidence in long-horizon contracts and is the main reason simple point ratings misprice the tails.

nhl.loser_point_rate.label: Loser-point and overtime-resolution rate by team
nhl.loser_point_rate.mechanism: Share of a team's games decided after regulation and its conditional win share.
nhl.loser_point_rate.rationale: Standings points include a point for an overtime or shootout loss, so two teams with equal win rates can differ in points by their extra-time frequency; regulation-win tiebreaks also depend on how often games are decided in regulation.
nhl.loser_point_rate.measurement: Per team and season compute: P(game goes beyond regulation) shrunk to league with k=30 games and 2-season weights; P(win | beyond regulation) shrunk to 0.5 with k=40 games (shootout/OT skill slight); regulation win rate from regulation results. Points per game = 2 x P(reg win) + 2 x P(extra) x p_win_extra + 1 x P(extra) x (1 - p_win_extra). Record regulation wins and ROW separately for tiebreak tracking.
raw_data: team-game result type (REG/OT/SO), points awarded, regulation wins
nhl.loser_point_rate.why: Maps game-level win probability into points and tiebreak counts, which the playoff boundary and Presidents' Trophy contracts depend on.

nhl.bracket_path_difficulty.label: Playoff bracket path difficulty by seed and division
nhl.bracket_path_difficulty.mechanism: Distribution of first and second round opponents and home-ice status given the final seed.
nhl.bracket_path_difficulty.rationale: The bracket pairs division winners with wild cards and keeps divisional paths, so equal-strength teams have different Cup and conference probabilities depending on their division and seed; the path must be simulated from standings.
nhl.bracket_path_difficulty.measurement: For each simulated final standings compute the bracket (3 per division plus 2 wild cards; division winner with better record faces the lower wild card) and the opponent set per round; record probabilities by team of facing each opponent and of home-ice in each series; use for series win recursion with rating uncertainty draws. Validate that simulated seed frequencies match historical qualifier frequencies by points.
raw_data: division membership, standings, format rules
nhl.bracket_path_difficulty.why: Turns qualification and seed into the opponent set that determines conference and Cup probability.

nhl.cap_flexibility_deadline.label: Cap flexibility and deadline additions capacity
nhl.cap_flexibility_deadline.mechanism: Cap space, long-term injured reserve relief and tradable assets that allow a team to add or replace players before the deadline.
nhl.cap_flexibility_deadline.rationale: A team's rating at the playoffs differs from today's rating through deadline moves and injury replacement; teams with cap room and assets can improve, which shifts long-horizon probabilities and is partially public.
nhl.cap_flexibility_deadline.measurement: From cap sites gather per team cap hit, projected deadline cap space (daily cap accrual x days remaining), LTIR usage, number of first-round picks and prospect capital (rank-based score from public prospect ratings); compute capacity = deadline space + LTIR relief; map to expected rating gain via historical deadline acquisitions of playoff contenders (average WAR added per cap dollar) with k=10 team-seasons; refresh weekly.
raw_data: team cap tables, LTIR status, pick inventory, trade logs
nhl.cap_flexibility_deadline.why: Adds a forward-looking component to ratings for contracts that resolve after the trade deadline.

nhl.series_goalie_volatility.label: Series-level goaltending volatility beyond binomial
nhl.series_goalie_volatility.mechanism: Extra variance of a series' save percentage and goal differential beyond a Bernoulli game model.
nhl.series_goalie_volatility.rationale: A best-of-seven series with fixed team ratings is binomial, but goalie performance autocorrelates within a series, producing a heavier-tailed distribution of series outcomes and more upsets than a constant p model gives.
nhl.series_goalie_volatility.measurement: From playoff series 2005-06 onward compute the series-level excess variance of goalie save percentage over binomial given shots faced; estimate intra-series correlation of single-game goalie GSAx; add a random effect on the winner's per-game p with sd estimated by maximum likelihood on series results; use in the series recursion. Shrink to league average with k=60 series.
raw_data: goalie-game shots, goals, GSAx; series outcomes
nhl.series_goalie_volatility.why: Short series are variance-dominated; this sets how far a rating gap translates to series win probability.

nhl.award_vote_share_model.label: Award vote-share model (electorate-specific)
nhl.award_vote_share_model.mechanism: Historical multinomial-logit model of vote shares for each award using production, team success, position and narrative variables.
nhl.award_vote_share_model.rationale: Hart, Norris and Calder are voted by writers and Vezina by general managers; each electorate rewards different features (points, team rank, goalie wins, shutouts, GSAx), so a single player-quality model does not map to voting outcomes.
nhl.award_vote_share_model.measurement: For each award collect the last 20 seasons' finalists and vote shares; regress log vote share on points per game, goals, team points percentage, games played, position and for goalies wins, save percentage and shutouts; fit multinomial logit with season fixed effects and shrinkage; apply to the projected end-of-season stat line distribution from simulations; output win probability by candidate with draw uncertainty; update with finalists and ballot dates.
raw_data: award voting results with candidates, vote points, season stats
nhl.award_vote_share_model.why: Needed for the six award and stat title contracts because they resolve by voters, not by team quality.

nhl.award_eligibility_tiebreak_map.label: Award eligibility and tiebreak rules map
nhl.award_eligibility_tiebreak_map.mechanism: Eligibility conditions and tiebreak rules for each trophy and stat title.
nhl.award_eligibility_tiebreak_map.rationale: Rookie eligibility for the Calder, the way Art Ross and Rocket Richard ties are broken and Kalshi's 1/N payout interact: a tied or ineligible candidate changes the contract value even if production is identical.
nhl.award_eligibility_tiebreak_map.measurement: For each award list eligibility criteria (age, prior NHL games) and the league's tiebreak (fewer games played or more goals for Art Ross) from the NHL rulebook or award page; label each as verified or SOURCE_UNVERIFIED; map to Kalshi tie handling (1/N rounded down) and compute the probability of ties for counting leaders from simulation (points ties at the top occur in a minority of seasons).
raw_data: award eligibility rules, tiebreak rules
nhl.award_eligibility_tiebreak_map.why: Defines who can win and what a tie pays, which matters in tight races.

nhl.xg_for.reason: Offensive component of the rating; useful as an ingredient, not a separate predictor beyond the rating.

nhl.xg_against.reason: Defensive component of the rating; same role as xg_for and should enter jointly with goaltending.

nhl.goalie_quality.reason: Largest single-player component of team strength especially in the playoffs, but GSAx persistence is low so shrinkage is essential.

nhl.injuries_pit.reason: Long-term injuries to key players change strength for months; the contract effect depends on replacement capacity, not the flag alone.

nhl.pdo_regression.reason: Regresses lucky standings before simulation; useful early in the season when records are driven by luck.

nhl.sos_remaining.reason: Remaining schedule changes points expectations modestly and matters only near the boundary of qualification.

nhl.standings_tiebreakers.reason: Regulation-win tiebreaks decide boundary and Presidents' Trophy ties and require tracking of regulation wins in the simulation.

nhl.series_context.reason: Only relevant once a series is underway; no series market is in this archetype now and in November it carries no information.

nhl.playoff_context.reason: Changes environment and format parameters of series simulation; a regime flag rather than a team feature.

nhl.news.reason: Trades and coaching changes shift strength after ratings are fitted; unstructured, so it is useful only after being converted to rating changes.

m.external_lines.reason: Sportsbook futures prices are a benchmark for comparison; using them as input contaminates a fundamentals-based forecast.

m.quote_history.reason: Kalshi's own price path reflects market beliefs; it is useful for studying news reaction, not as a causal input.

nhl.season_sim_distribution.reason: The ratings label already includes season simulation; the simulation is a procedure applied to ratings and tiebreak rules, not a separate input.

interactions.mechanism: Title probability is a convex function of team rating, so rating uncertainty raises the probability of mid-tier teams and lowers that of favourites relative to a point-rating simulation; the effect is strongest early in the season and fades as the posterior tightens.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate with and without rating draws and compare Cup probabilities by seed and across horizons.

interactions.mechanism: A seven-game series amplifies single-game randomness and goalie volatility compounds with series length: the same rating gap yields a lower win probability than a constant-p recursion would give once goalie autocorrelation is included.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit series outcomes with and without a random goalie effect and compare upset frequency.

interactions.mechanism: Regulation wins are the first tiebreaker, so two teams with equal points but different loser-point counts have different qualification odds; the effect arises only at ties and is conditional on the points boundary.
interactions.how_to_test: Count playoff outcomes of tied-on-points teams by regulation wins over history and compare with a points-only model.

interactions.mechanism: A long-term injury to a key player reduces rating, but a team with cap space and assets can replace part of the loss before the deadline, so the effect on a futures price is conditional on capacity and on the date of the injury.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare change in end-of-season rating after star injuries for teams with high and low capacity.

interactions.mechanism: Seed and division create path differences: a division winner plays a wild card while the other seeds meet inside the division; at the boundary between third seed and wild card, the path regime switches, so marginal points have an outsized effect on conference and Cup odds.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute conference and Cup probabilities for the same rating under each of the possible seed placements and compare.

interactions.mechanism: For voted awards a candidate's missing a month of games reduces his production below a threshold at which writers discount him; award probability falls in steps with games missed more than linearly with games lost.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare vote share of finalists by games missed using 20 seasons of results.

nonlinearities.shape: Convex in rating for championship probability
nonlinearities.why: Winning four best-of-seven rounds multiplies four probabilities, so a small rating advantage compounds; the title odds of the top team rise faster than linearly with rating and the odds of weak qualifiers fall faster than linearly.

nonlinearities.shape: Logistic around the playoff points cut-off
nonlinearities.why: Qualification is a threshold event: the probability moves from near zero to near one over a range of about 10-15 points around the mid-90s cut-off, so small changes in expected points matter most for bubble teams.

nonlinearities.shape: Decreasing in games played
nonlinearities.why: Posterior sd of rating falls roughly with the inverse square root of games played plus a drift floor, so the uncertainty premium for long-horizon futures is largest now and decays through the season.

contract.settlement_definition: KXNHLADAMS pays YES if the named head coach wins the NHL Jack Adams Award for the 2026-27 season; if multiple participants tie for the award, Yes positions pay $1/N rounded down to the nearest cent and No pays $1 minus that. KXNHLDRAFTTOP (top pick) and KXNHLDRAFTPICK (draft pick) are draft-selection contracts that currently list no markets and have no rules text, so their year, definition of the pick, and treatment of trades or ties is unseen. The ledger files draft contracts and a coach award here though the archetype label describes player awards and season stat leaders.

rules_evidence.quote: If Todd McLellan wins the NHL Jack Adams Award in the 2026-27 NHL season, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: The contract resolves on the league's announced winner of the Jack Adams Award for the 2026-27 season; the winner is chosen by voters, so no statistic settles it.

rules_evidence.quote: positions will pay $1/N (rounded down to the nearest cent), where N is the number of tied participants
rules_evidence.establishes: A tied award pays a fractional amount to each tied winner, so the contract is a share-of-prize payoff in tie cases rather than pure binary.

variants_and_edge_cases: Coach versus player awards: the only live award series here is for a head coach, who can be fired or replaced mid-season, a case the sampled text does not address (whether an interim coach or a coach who left can win is unspecified).

Draft contracts: KXNHLDRAFTTOP and KXNHLDRAFTPICK have no listed markets, so the draft year, whether 'top pick' means first overall selection, and how a traded pick or a pick number tie is handled are unknown.

Timing: the ballots for league awards are cast at the end of the regular season and winners are announced weeks later, so information after the ballot deadline cannot affect the outcome, while information before it flows only through the voters' perception.
Ties: the sampled tie rule applies to awards; ties are rare for voted awards but possible, and draft contracts could have no tie concept at all.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official NHL award announcements (league and award-voting bodies); draft selections from the league's official draft record.

mechanism.summary: The three live contracts in this archetype resolve through decisions rather than through a counting statistic. The Jack Adams Award is a vote on a head coach, and voters reward exceeding expectation (a team that improves sharply or beats its preseason projection) rather than the best team in absolute terms; so the outcome is a function of the gap between realised and expected team results, the coaching story (first-year coach, turnaround, injury adversity), and the timing of ballots. The draft contracts are two-step processes: the standings determine lottery odds for non-playoff teams (and ownership of the pick determines who benefits), and the selecting team chooses from a pool whose order is known with high but not complete consensus. Neither process is well represented by the player-production inputs in the existing entry, so the main task is to define the missing coach-expectation, lottery, ownership and prospect-consensus inputs.

stages.name: Candidate pool and eligibility
stages.description: For a coach award the pool is every head coach in office long enough in the season, with mid-season firings and interim coaches changing eligibility; the favourites are coaches whose teams currently beat preseason projection. For the draft the pool is the draft-eligible class, with a small set of top prospects and uncertainty over eligibility year, injuries and developmental paths. The pool structure restricts who can resolve YES at all.
stages.distribution: Short list of 3-6 serious candidates with heavy-tailed probabilities; the remaining candidates share a small residual.

stages.name: Performance relative to expectation (coaching award)
stages.description: The award rewards over-performance: realised points percentage minus what a preseason projection predicted, the year-over-year change, and whether the team did it despite injuries or roster loss. Team strength estimates and their uncertainty determine the expected result; the outcome distribution of final points is wide (sd of 7-9 points), so a leader in November is only mildly informative about the final ranking of coaches.
stages.distribution: Final points of each team ~ Gaussian around the projection with sd 7-9; the coach ranking is the ranking of expectation gaps, so the maximum of many noisy gaps.

stages.name: Electorate, ballot timing and narrative
stages.description: Voters weigh narrative as much as the numbers: first-year coaches, turnarounds and managing through injuries; the electorate (a specific broadcasters' association, to be verified) casts ballots at the end of the regular season, so what happens in the playoffs is irrelevant and the finalist list narrows to three. Award timing introduces step changes in information when finalists are named.
stages.distribution: Multinomial choice over finalists with a few candidates holding most mass; vote shares typically spread across 3 finalists.

stages.name: Draft lottery, pick ownership and selection
stages.description: The draft top pick depends on which team has the pick and what it selects: non-playoff teams enter a lottery whose odds follow final standings (the worst team has the highest chance, with caps on how far a team can rise), the pick may belong to another team through trades or be protected, and the team on the clock picks from a prospect board in which the consensus first choice is selected most of the time. Each step is a separate probability and they multiply.
stages.distribution: Lottery: categorical over teams with probabilities from 18 percent down to under 1 percent; selection given pick: categorical over prospects with a leading consensus candidate near 0.7-0.9 for a clear top prospect.

opponent_matchup.note: The contracts resolve on season-long outcomes and a draft selection, not on matchups between teams or players; no pairing mechanism applies.

environment.note: Rink, weather and travel conditions have no direct effect on a coach vote or a draft selection beyond their small influence on team results, which the ratings already contain.

pace_volume.note: No counting volume (shots, possessions, plate appearances) settles an award vote or a draft pick; the nearest analogue is games played in a season, which is covered by the ratings and injury inputs.

efficiency_conversion.note: Shooting or save conversion matters for team success, but the contracts resolve on voters' and teams' choices rather than a rate statistic, so conversion enters only through expected points inside the rating.

officiating_rules.note: Officiating has no bearing on a coach vote or draft selection; the only rule-like element is lottery and eligibility rules, handled as settlement inputs.

nhl.coach_expectation_delta.label: Coach expectation delta (results versus preseason projection, year-over-year change)
nhl.coach_expectation_delta.mechanism: Difference between realised points percentage and the preseason-projected value, plus year-over-year change and coaching tenure flags.
nhl.coach_expectation_delta.rationale: The Jack Adams Award is voted on who coached best relative to expectations, so what matters is the surprise, not the level; a team that finished first as expected earns less credit than one that jumped from the bottom. The expectation must be formed before the season to avoid hindsight bias.
nhl.coach_expectation_delta.measurement: Preseason projection P_exp = last two seasons' points percentage blend (0.6/0.4) adjusted by roster change impact and age; delta = realised points pct to date (or simulated final) minus P_exp, with standard error from remaining games; add change from last season, first-year-coach flag, injury games lost to key players, and goalie change flag. Fit a ranking model of historical winners/finalists on delta and these flags (20 seasons) and output candidate win probabilities with simulation draws for final points.
raw_data: team season points pct, preseason projections, coach tenure, injury games lost
nhl.coach_expectation_delta.why: The core of the Jack Adams voter model and absent from the draft's player-production inputs.

nhl.draft_lottery_odds_by_standing.label: Draft lottery odds by final standing and ownership
nhl.draft_lottery_odds_by_standing.mechanism: Probability each team wins the top pick from the simulated final standings and the league lottery format.
nhl.draft_lottery_odds_by_standing.rationale: The first pick is not simply given to the worst team: the lottery format gives the worst team a limited chance and caps how far a team can move, so the distribution is flat over the bottom teams and depends on exact standings and on the number of draws.
nhl.draft_lottery_odds_by_standing.measurement: Simulate final standings from the ratings posterior (with points ties resolved by league rules), identify the 16 non-playoff teams, map rank to lottery combinations using the current published format (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for 2027) with ranges for odds of first pick and for the maximum movement allowed; combine with pick ownership to get P(team T holds the first pick) = sum over teams of P(team wins lottery) x ownership; output with the standings uncertainty.
raw_data: simulated standings, lottery combination table, lottery history
nhl.draft_lottery_odds_by_standing.why: Provides the first stage of the top-pick contract: which team will be on the clock.

nhl.pick_ownership_and_protection.label: First-round pick ownership and protection conditions
nhl.pick_ownership_and_protection.mechanism: Which team holds each first-round pick with its protections and conditionality.
nhl.pick_ownership_and_protection.rationale: Traded picks, top-ten protections and conditional swaps change who benefits from a bad finish; a lottery winner that has traded its pick selects nothing, so ownership multiplies the lottery probability.
nhl.pick_ownership_and_protection.measurement: Collect the first-round pick table for the draft year with owner, original team, protection (top-N, lottery), and conditions (swap rights), from PuckPedia/CapWages and official transaction records; version it by date; encode as owner(team) and conditional logic evaluated on the simulated standings; track changes after each trade.
raw_data: pick inventory with owner, protections, conditions, dates
nhl.pick_ownership_and_protection.why: Determines which franchise's selection a top-pick contract depends on, with conditionality evaluated on simulated standings.

nhl.prospect_consensus_ranking.label: Prospect consensus ranking and selection agreement history
nhl.prospect_consensus_ranking.mechanism: Consensus ordering of top prospects and the historical probability that the consensus choice is selected at each pick.
nhl.prospect_consensus_ranking.rationale: The selecting team's choice follows a board that correlates strongly with public consensus at the very top, with more disagreement later; a clear gap between the first and second prospects makes the top-pick contract nearly a one-candidate event.
nhl.prospect_consensus_ranking.measurement: Aggregate public rankings (NHL Central Scouting final list, Elite Prospects consensus, Bob McKenzie/TSN list, others) into a rank-averaged score, compute the gap between first and second; calibrate P(consensus #1 is selected first) from 15 drafts as a function of gap with a logistic fit; for later picks use rank deviation distributions; update with injuries and with team-specific needs flags.
raw_data: public rankings by date, historical draft results
nhl.prospect_consensus_ranking.why: Gives the second stage of the draft contracts: what the team on the clock does.

nhl.award_stats.reason: Player production to date does not drive a coach award or a draft selection; it applies to Hart or stat-leader contracts that sit under the futures archetype.

nhl.award_voting_rules.reason: The electorate, ballot timing and finalists define when information can matter; needs the Jack Adams voting body and timing verified.

nhl.toi_trend.reason: Ice-time trends of players are a skater-level input and have no connection to a coach vote or draft pick.

nhl.pp_role.reason: Power-play unit role is a skater production driver, not related to a coach award or draft selection.

nhl.ixg_player.reason: Individual expected goals of skaters bears on player awards but not on the coach award or draft; it contaminates the entry for these live series.

nhl.finishing.reason: Player finishing regression is relevant for player scoring leaders only; no live contract in this archetype uses it.

nhl.goalie_quality.reason: Goaltending influences team results and therefore the coach's expectation delta, but it is a component of the team rating rather than a separate predictor of the vote.

nhl.career_trajectory.reason: Age curves for skaters do not map to a coach vote; it might help evaluating draft prospects' development but that is not its definition here.

nhl.injuries_pit.reason: Injuries to key players set the expectation against which the coach is judged and can create an adversity narrative.

nhl.ratings.reason: Team strength and the standing relative to preseason expectation underlie the coach vote and set the lottery odds, but the entry must combine it with the expectation delta.

nhl.announcement_calendar.reason: Ballot, finalist and draft dates determine which information is incorporated; useful as a timing mask.

nhl.news.reason: Coach firings, trades and eligibility news change the candidate set; unstructured and sparse.

nhl.stat_dist.reason: Count distributions of player stats are not what these contracts depend on; for team points a normal approximation is adequate.

interactions.mechanism: A coach's vote probability depends on over-performance conditional on adversity: a team beating projection while missing top players is valued above the same delta with a healthy roster, so injuries amplify the narrative only when the team is still above expectation.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit historical finalists on delta with an interaction with injury games lost and check coefficient sign.

interactions.mechanism: P(team T holds the first pick) = P(T wins the lottery) x P(T owns its pick), and both depend on the simulated standings jointly; a traded pick with protections makes ownership a function of the same standings that determine lottery odds.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate standings and evaluate lottery and ownership logic in the same draw and compare with the product of marginals.

interactions.mechanism: The consensus first prospect is selected unless the team on the clock has a specific need or the prospect is injured, so the selection probability is conditional on the owner of the pick and on news; clear gaps in consensus make this conditional weak.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare selection of the consensus first prospect by gap size and by team need flags over 15 drafts.

interactions.mechanism: Information after the ballot deadline cannot change the vote, so the effect of late-season form on the award is zero beyond the cut-off date, whereas before it each point of final points shifts candidate probabilities; the timing creates a threshold in the usefulness of data.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare award outcomes against standings at the ballot date versus at season end across 15 seasons.

interactions.mechanism: Late in the season teams out of the playoff race may lose games to improve lottery position only up to the point where the lottery caps rise; below that the benefit of extra losses is small, so the final standings of bottom teams carry weaker information than the points total suggests.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare lottery outcomes of teams by rank to test how flat the odds are among the bottom five.

nonlinearities.shape: Concave in final rank with caps
nonlinearities.why: Lottery odds fall from about 18 percent for the worst team to near 1 percent for the best non-playoff team and the caps on movement flatten the top, so rank is a non-linear map to the chance of winning the first pick.

nonlinearities.shape: Threshold for finalist selection
nonlinearities.why: A coach with a delta below roughly one to two standard errors of the leaders is rarely among the three finalists, so the vote probability is near zero below a threshold and rises steeply above it.

nonlinearities.shape: Logistic in the gap between first and second prospect
nonlinearities.why: When the consensus gap is large the selection is near certain; as the gap narrows toward zero the probability falls toward one half, a sigmoid response rather than a linear one.

contract.settlement_definition: Three unrelated event types share this archetype. KXNHLLINDSAY pays YES if the named player wins the 2026-27 Ted Lindsay Award, with ties paying $1/N rounded down. KXNHLNEXTTEAM pays YES for the named team if it is the player's next team before the stated date (the sample is 'before Nov 1, 2026'); a player who retires or has no team resolves to a 'Retires / No Team' contract, a player who remains on his issuance team resolves that team, and signing with any team including the previous one counts. KXNHLEXPANSION pays YES if the NHL officially announces an expansion franchise award to a named city before Jan 1, 2027, requiring formal approval naming the city.

rules_evidence.quote: The league must officially announce that the city has been awarded an expansion franchise.
rules_evidence.establishes: Resolution needs an official league announcement of a franchise award; reports, stadium approvals and feasibility studies do not count, so insider reports are not settlement events.

rules_evidence.quote: If Quinn Hughes remains on the team they were on upon issuance on Nov 1, 2026, then the market for that team will resolve Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: Staying put resolves the incumbent team's market, so the default outcome is the status quo and the contract is about the probability of a change of team inside the window.

rules_evidence.quote: positions will pay $1/N (rounded down to the nearest cent), where N is the number of tied participants
rules_evidence.establishes: The award contract is voted by an electorate and pays 1/N on ties; the outcome is not a statistic.

variants_and_edge_cases: Three different generating processes: a player-voted award, a free-agent/transaction destination (a multi-outcome partition over 32 teams plus retire/no team) and a governance event (expansion approval by the Board of Governors), so a single base rate cannot cover them.

Next-team window: the sampled market is 'before Nov 1, 2026', a date already passed on the review date (Nov 7, 2026), so the sample is stale or expired; the text 'is a free agent ... for any period of time' means a re-signing with the same team counts as YES for that team after free agency.
Expansion contract requires the announcement to come after market issuance and to name the city; relocation counts only if designated expansion, and the team need not begin play before the date.
Award variants: the Ted Lindsay Award is voted by the players' association (to be verified), a different electorate from the writers' awards, so features that predict Hart do not map directly.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official NHL and NHLPA announcements for awards and expansion; NHL transaction records for next team.

mechanism.summary: These markets are not produced by on-ice play; they are produced by institutions with calendars, constraints and information channels. For a destination market the outcome is a draw from a discrete set of teams constrained by the player's contract status (expiry year, no-move clauses, signing windows), by the cap space and needs of potential suitors, and by the time window; the default is the status quo and the main hazard is concentrated at a few calendar points. For a governance event like expansion the outcome requires a formal board decision after preparatory steps (city readiness, ownership, arena, fee, announced timeline), so the event is gated by the calendar of meetings. For a voted award the outcome is a multinomial choice by a specific electorate. In all cases information arrives through insider reports that are informative but not settling events, so the model must weight credibility and lag between report and official announcement.

stages.name: Event class and reference-class hazard
stages.description: Each contract is first placed in a reference class with its own base rate: a star defenceman changing teams within a given window, a league expanding within a year, a player winning a peer-voted trophy. The reference class must be narrow because pooling destination, governance and voting events gives meaningless base rates. The hazard inside the window depends on how many calendar events fall within it.
stages.distribution: Rare event with a time-varying hazard; for destination markets the base probability of a move inside a short window is a few percent for incumbents under contract and high for free agents at the market open.

stages.name: Institutional gates and constraints
stages.description: A player can only move if his contract allows it: expiry, no-trade and no-move lists, signing windows and arbitration status define the set of feasible destinations; suitors need cap space and roster room. An expansion award needs a Board of Governors approval after an expansion process, which is only possible at a scheduled meeting or special session. The contract wording decides what counts (official announcement, signing, not reports).
stages.distribution: Feasible-set logic: the destination distribution is supported on a subset of teams; governance outcomes are gated binary events conditional on a meeting.

stages.name: Information flow from insiders to official announcements
stages.description: Public reports from league insiders arrive before official announcements and move beliefs, but their reliability varies by reporter and report type (pending talks versus agreed terms); the lag between the report and the official step determines how much of the hazard is realised inside the contract window. Rules requiring an official announcement make unconfirmed reports non-settling.
stages.distribution: Bayesian update with report-specific likelihood ratios; lag between report and announcement ranges from hours to months with heavy tails.

stages.name: Electorate choice for voted awards
stages.description: The Ted Lindsay contract is a multinomial outcome decided by a player electorate whose ballots are private, so the model relies on production, reputation, previous winners and team success as proxies; the vote correlates with writers' awards but is not identical. The ballot timing and finalist announcements create step changes in information.
stages.distribution: Multinomial logit over a small set of finalists; vote shares overlap and ties are possible.

coaching_scheme.note: None of the contracts depend on on-ice tactics or coaching systems; the destination of a player can be influenced by a coach, but only as part of the news signal.

environment.note: Venue and travel conditions do not drive a transaction, an award or a governance decision; the only environmental factor is arena readiness for expansion, handled in the governance input.

game_context_script.note: No game state or score path affects these events, which resolve through institutional processes rather than within-game play.

pace_volume.note: There is no counting process of plays or shots behind these contracts; the only volume-like quantity is the number of calendar opportunities in the window, covered by the calendar input.

efficiency_conversion.note: No conversion rate (shooting, saving) settles these contracts; production only enters the Lindsay vote through the award model.

officiating_rules.note: No on-ice officiating applies; the rules that matter are the settlement text and league governance procedures, covered under the contract and governance inputs.

nhl.player_contract_status_clauses.label: Player contract status and movement clauses
nhl.player_contract_status_clauses.mechanism: Contract expiry year, cap hit, no-trade or no-move clauses, arbitration and free-agent status for the named player.
nhl.player_contract_status_clauses.rationale: Destination markets are bounded by the contract: a player under a long contract with a no-movement clause can only move with consent, while a player on an expiring contract becomes a free agent on a known date; the same inputs determine whether any team can acquire him at all.
nhl.player_contract_status_clauses.measurement: For the player compile from cap sites: contract end year, AAV, NMC/NTC status and no-trade list if public, RFA/UFA status and arbitration rights, extension eligibility date, and the signing/trade windows of the NHL calendar; compute months to free agency and an indicator of whether a trade requires consent; refresh weekly and after each transaction; encode a feasible destination set with ex ante constraint flags.
raw_data: player contracts with clauses and dates, league calendar
nhl.player_contract_status_clauses.why: Sets the support of the destination distribution and the timing of movement for the next-team contract.

nhl.suitor_cap_and_roster_fit.label: Suitor cap space and roster-fit table
nhl.suitor_cap_and_roster_fit.mechanism: Cap space, positional need and competitive window of each team relative to the player.
nhl.suitor_cap_and_roster_fit.rationale: A destination requires cap room and a lineup need; teams with space and a hole at the position are the likely suitors, and the number of feasible suitors changes the probabilities in a partition over 32 teams.
nhl.suitor_cap_and_roster_fit.measurement: For each team compute projected cap space at the next signing window (cap ceiling minus committed salary for the next season, adjusted for LTIR), roster need for the position (depth chart gap in impact score), and a competitive-window score (points percentage and age of core); form a suitor score = space feasibility x need x window with weights fit on past star free-agent decisions (5 seasons, k=15 events); normalise to a probability vector with the player's preference (location, prior team) if known.
raw_data: team cap tables, roster depth by position
nhl.suitor_cap_and_roster_fit.why: Provides the probability vector across teams that the contract's partition requires.

nhl.expansion_governance_gates.label: Expansion governance gates and readiness checklist
nhl.expansion_governance_gates.mechanism: Calendar of Board of Governors meetings and the readiness steps (ownership group, arena, fee, committee statements) for a candidate city.
nhl.expansion_governance_gates.rationale: An expansion award requires an official Board decision, which cannot occur without an expansion process and a meeting; the hazard of a decision before a given date is the probability that these gates are cleared in time.
nhl.expansion_governance_gates.measurement: Record the scheduled Board of Governors meeting dates before the market close, the public status of the expansion process (committee formed, applications requested, ownership group named, arena plan, expansion fee level) and commissioner statements with dates; assign a stage score (0-5) and map stage to the probability of a vote before the date using historical expansion cases (Vegas 2016, Seattle 2018, Utah transfer) with wide uncertainty; update after each public statement.
raw_data: dated governance statements, meeting calendar, bid status
nhl.expansion_governance_gates.why: Defines whether the formal decision step can occur inside the window, which dominates the probability for the expansion contract.

nhl.insider_report_credibility.label: Insider report credibility and lag
nhl.insider_report_credibility.mechanism: Reporter- and report-type-specific hit rate and lag between a report and the official announcement.
nhl.insider_report_credibility.rationale: Reports of talks, offers or agreements differ in reliability; the contract only settles on official actions, so the hit rate and lag set how much a report should move the probability within the time window.
nhl.insider_report_credibility.measurement: Collect reports by named insiders on transactions for 5 seasons with report type (talks, close, agreed, official), then label outcomes (official within 7, 30, 90 days); compute per-reporter and per-type hit rate with Beta(2,2) prior and the distribution of lag; convert to likelihood ratio of a report for the contract's event within its window; store report timestamp and wording.
free_sources: Public posts of NHL insiders (own capture)
raw_data: dated insider reports with type and later official outcomes
nhl.insider_report_credibility.why: Controls the weight to put on news in markets that settle only on official events.

nhl.award_vote_share_model.label: Award vote-share model (electorate-specific)
nhl.award_vote_share_model.mechanism: Historical multinomial-logit model of vote shares for each award using production, team success, position and narrative variables.
nhl.award_vote_share_model.rationale: Hart, Norris and Calder are voted by writers and Vezina by general managers; each electorate rewards different features (points, team rank, goalie wins, shutouts, GSAx), so a single player-quality model does not map to voting outcomes.
nhl.award_vote_share_model.measurement: For each award collect the last 20 seasons' finalists and vote shares; regress log vote share on points per game, goals, team points percentage, games played, position and for goalies wins, save percentage and shutouts; fit multinomial logit with season fixed effects and shrinkage; apply to the projected end-of-season stat line distribution from simulations; output win probability by candidate with draw uncertainty; update with finalists and ballot dates.
raw_data: award voting results with candidates, vote points, season stats
nhl.award_vote_share_model.why: The Ted Lindsay Award is voted by an electorate different from the writers' awards, so the vote-share model must be fit separately with peer-vote proxies, but the same structure (finalists, production, team success, reputation) applies.

nhl.offfield_base_rate.reason: A single pooled base rate for destination, governance and award events is meaningless; each class needs its own narrow reference class and time-varying hazard.

nhl.announcement_calendar.reason: Fixed league dates (free agency, trade windows, Board meetings, award ceremonies) concentrate the hazard and bound feasible dates.

nhl.news.reason: Insider reporting is the main information channel, but unstructured news needs a credibility and lag model to be usable.

m.rules_text.reason: Settlement requires official announcements and defines what counts as the next team, tie payoffs and retirement outcomes.

m.quote_history.reason: Price reaction after reports measures the market's reading of news and is the quantity to be compared, not a causal input.

m.volume_oi.reason: Volume and open interest describe the market's liquidity; they say nothing about whether the event will occur.

m.lifecycle.reason: Close time and open date define how much of the hazard lies inside the window and when the market stops; this is a rule-derived input.

m.external_lines.reason: Sportsbook or exchange prices on these events, if they exist, are benchmarks and must not be features for a fundamentals model.

m.strike_hit_rates.reason: Historical settled frequencies on Kalshi for these novelty contracts are tiny samples and are outcomes of the market itself, not causes.

interactions.mechanism: Hazard is concentrated at calendar points (free agency opening, trade windows, Board meetings), so the probability of an event inside a window is the sum of mass at the dated gates inside it, not a constant hazard times duration.
interactions.how_to_test: Build the calendar of gate dates inside the window and compare realised event timing over past seasons with a constant-hazard model.

interactions.mechanism: A report of an agreement raises probability, but the contract settles only on an official step and a lag between the two, so the effect depends on the credibility of the source and on whether the official step falls before the contract closes.
interactions.how_to_test: Label past reports by type and measure the share followed by the official action within the window length.

interactions.mechanism: A destination needs both a feasible contract status (consent, expiry, window) and a suitor with space and need; the probability for a team is the product of feasibility and fit, so a team with ideal fit but a closed window has nearly zero probability.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare realised destinations with the product of feasibility and fit scores versus fit alone over past star moves.

interactions.mechanism: Expansion before the deadline requires an expansion process to have reached a Board vote; unless a meeting with the vote is scheduled inside the window the probability is near zero, a threshold on the governance stage rather than a gradual hazard.
interactions.how_to_test: Record the stage of past expansion bids at each month before announcement and compare with the time to the Board vote.

interactions.mechanism: Vote shares for peer-voted awards are shared among a few finalists and ties pay 1/N, so the win probability of each candidate and the tie mass come from the same multinomial; peer votes correlate with writers' votes but with different weights on reputation.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit separate vote-share models for peer-voted and writer-voted awards and compare weights on points, team success and reputation.

nonlinearities.shape: Spiked hazard at dated gates
nonlinearities.why: Free agency opening and trade deadlines produce a very high short-term hazard compared with the remainder of the window, so the probability of a change of team is a step function of calendar position, not linear in time.

nonlinearities.shape: Convex in proximity to contract expiry
nonlinearities.why: The probability a player moves rises sharply in the final contract year and at the free-agency date; years remaining is a convex, non-linear predictor, and clauses create hard zeros for non-consenting destinations.

nonlinearities.shape: Logistic in report type and source reliability
nonlinearities.why: A report of agreed terms from a reliable source moves the probability close to one while a report of talks barely moves it; the map from report to probability is sigmoid in a credibility score.
