contract.settlement_definition: Season-long counting contracts resolved on official 2026-27 regular-season records: KXNHLPSEASONGOALS and KXNHLSEASONGOALS pay YES if the named player scores at least the stated number of goals (for example 60 or 40) during the regular season; KXNHLSEASONPTS pays YES if the named team earns at least the stated standings points (95), points being awarded for wins and for overtime or shootout losses; KXNHLATLANTIC, METROPOLITAN, CENTRAL and PACIFIC pay YES if the named team wins its division; KXNHLWSTREAK pays YES if the team has the longest winning streak in the regular season, ties paying $1/(number of tied teams) rounded down. Playoff results are excluded where stated.

rules_evidence.quote: official NHL standings points, awarded for wins and overtime or shootout losses in the 2026-27 NHL regular season
rules_evidence.establishes: Team points follow the league's three-point-game system, so the total includes loser points, which are partly noise and affect the threshold more than win count alone.

rules_evidence.quote: If Macklin Celebrini scores at least 60 goals during the 2026-27 NHL regular season, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: A season goal total threshold with a floor_strike of 59.5; the quantity is games played times goal rate, and no game-played minimum or trade clause is stated.

rules_evidence.quote: then the markets for each of those tied teams will resolve to $1/(the number of tied teams), rounded down
rules_evidence.establishes: A tie for the longest winning streak pays 1/N, so the contract is an extremum-of-32 statistic with dead-heat tie handling; the definition of a winning streak (overtime wins) is not stated.

rules_evidence.quote: If the Toronto Maple Leafs win the 2026-27 NHL Atlantic Division, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: Division winner contracts carry no secondary rules text, so the tiebreak for the division title (points, then regulation wins) is not stated in the sample.

variants_and_edge_cases: Six of the eight live series are team-level (four division winners, a team points total, a longest win streak) and only two are player goal totals; the 'All-NHL team' contract type in the blueprint has no live series and no text.

Player goal totals: the official goals statistic counts empty-net and overtime goals but shootout goals are recorded separately, a point not covered by the text; a traded player keeps his total; no minimum games clause is stated.
Division winner contracts have an empty secondary rule: tiebreaks (regulation wins or ROW) are unseen, so close races carry settlement ambiguity; ties for the longest streak follow the 1/N rule.
Strike construction differs: goals use 'at least N' with floor_strike N-0.5, team points use 'greater_or_equal' 95, and division and streak contracts are structured outright partitions over teams.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official NHL regular-season statistics and standings (goals, points, division standings, streak records).

mechanism.summary: Season counting contracts are sums over a fixed schedule, so the outcome is a rate times opportunities with uncertainty in both. For a player's goal total the rate is shots per game times shooting percentage, each with a talent component and a luck component, the opportunities are games played (zero-inflated by injuries and rest) and minutes (role, power-play share), and the league scoring environment shifts everyone. Early in the season the to-date total is only a small piece of the total, so the talent prior and the age trajectory dominate. For team points the unit is the 82-game points sum with loser points; division winner is the maximum over a handful of teams with tiebreaks that reward regulation wins; the longest winning streak is the maximum over 32 teams of a run-length statistic whose tail depends on the best teams' win probability and on streakiness (goalie form, schedule). Settlement ties pay 1/N, and some tiebreaks are unseen.

stages.name: Talent prior and rate decomposition for the player
stages.description: A player's goal rate per game equals shot volume per game times shooting percentage. Shot volume is the most stable component and is anchored by shot rate per 60 and ice time; shooting percentage regresses strongly toward a player-specific talent estimate built from xG per shot. Age curves shift both and early-season data are weighted lightly. This stage produces the rate distribution for the rest of the season, not a point estimate.
stages.distribution: Rate distribution with posterior sd of order 10-15 percent of the mean for established scorers; shooting percentage has a binomial noise component of order sd 2.5-3 points over a season.

stages.name: Opportunity: games played, minutes and power-play role
stages.description: The number of games played is capped at 82 and reduced by injury and rest; for a star, the distribution has most mass at 78-82 and a long left tail from injuries. Minutes and PP unit role set the volume per game, and PP1 membership is more persistent than even-strength points. A player on a high-scoring PP unit has a rate floor that survives regression. These opportunities convert linearly into goals once the rate is fixed.
stages.distribution: Games played: 82 minus a zero-inflated heavy-tailed missed-games count (about 10-15 percent chance of missing 15+ games for veterans).

stages.name: Accumulation, to-date information and thresholds
stages.description: The season total is goals to date plus a rest-of-season sum; with about 68 games remaining the remaining sum is a compound count with random rate and random games. A threshold such as 60 goals (floor 59.5) requires a rate near 0.75 per game over 80 games; the probability is a steep function of the mean because the sd of a season total is only 7-8 goals. The league scoring environment also moves the mean for all players together.
stages.distribution: Season goals ~ negative binomial or compound Poisson with mean mu and sd about sqrt(mu) times 1.2 plus rate and games uncertainty; P(>=60) moves from 10 to 60 percent as mu goes from 52 to 60.

stages.name: Team points, division race and extremum statistics
stages.description: Team points are a sum of 82 results with two points for any win and one for an extra-time loss; the rating posterior (with uncertainty) and the remaining schedule give the expected points, and division winner is the maximum over a few correlated teams with tiebreaks that favour regulation wins. The longest win streak is an extremum over all teams of run lengths whose tail is driven by the best teams' per-game win probability and by streakiness from goalie form and schedule clustering; it needs a run-length model rather than a points model.
stages.distribution: Points total approximately Gaussian with sd 7-9; division winner as argmax over correlated Gaussian totals; longest streak as the maximum of 32 run-length geometric-type variables with tail exponent set by win probability.

stages.name: Settlement mapping and ties
stages.description: Resolution uses official counts: goals credited to the skater (excluding shootout goals), points from standings, division winner from final standings with the league tiebreak, and streak length from the league's record with 1/N on ties. The strike construction (floor 59.5 versus 'at least 60'; 95 inclusive) and the absence of text for division tiebreaks affect probabilities in tight cases.
stages.distribution: Discrete thresholds on integer counts; dead-heat 1/N payouts on ties; boundary events have positive probability mass.

coaching_scheme.note: Coaching systems affect a player's season total only through ice time, PP unit and linemates, which are modelled as role inputs; team-level contracts are driven by ratings that already include coaching effects.

game_context_script.note: Single-game script (score effects, empty-net timing) averages out across 82 games and enters season counts only through small average effects on rates; no game-level mechanism is needed for season totals.

officiating_rules.note: Penalty-calling tendencies affect season power-play opportunities, but their season-level effect is absorbed in the league scoring environment and team PP share, so no separate officiating input is needed.

nhl.games_played_hazard.label: Games-played hazard (injury, rest and load management)
nhl.games_played_hazard.mechanism: Distribution of games missed for a player over the season given age, position, injury history and team situation.
nhl.games_played_hazard.rationale: A season total is capped by games played; a 60-goal pace needs about 78-82 games, so the left tail from injuries is the main downside. A distribution (not an expected value) is needed because missing a month removes the contract's chances.
nhl.games_played_hazard.measurement: From 10 seasons of player-game logs compute for each skater-season games missed, then fit a zero-inflated negative binomial for games missed with covariates age, position, prior-season games missed (weights 0.5/0.3/0.2), prior major injury count, and current injury status; update for the current season with games already played and the current injury report; shrink toward position-age cohort with k=25 player-seasons; output the pmf of games remaining played given status.
free_sources: Man Games Lost datasets (paid) or injury trackers
raw_data: player-season games played, injury reports with dates, ages
nhl.games_played_hazard.why: Opportunity cap for all player season counting contracts, and the source of the left tail of the goal total.

nhl.win_streak_extremum_dist.label: Winning-streak extremum distribution (league-wide max run length)
nhl.win_streak_extremum_dist.mechanism: Probability distribution of the longest winning streak among 32 teams over the season, and per-team shares.
nhl.win_streak_extremum_dist.rationale: The longest streak is an extremum, determined by the best teams' win probability and by streakiness; modelling teams one at a time with independent geometric runs underestimates the maximum when goalie form and schedule clusters create autocorrelation.
nhl.win_streak_extremum_dist.measurement: Simulate seasons from the rating posterior (with per-game win probabilities, drift and a goalie-form autocorrelation parameter estimated from historical runs: lag-1 correlation of results controlling for strength, k=600 games); for each simulation record each team's longest regular-season streak counting regulation, OT and shootout wins as wins unless the rules say otherwise; output per-team probability of holding the maximum (with 1/N for ties). Calibrate against 20 seasons of league-max streak lengths.
raw_data: team-game results with date, win flag, OT/SO flag
nhl.win_streak_extremum_dist.why: The only contract in the archetype that depends on a run-length extremum rather than a total.

nhl.league_scoring_environment.label: League scoring environment drift
nhl.league_scoring_environment.mechanism: Current-season league goals per game relative to the prior-season baseline, with shrinkage.
nhl.league_scoring_environment.rationale: League scoring levels shift between seasons by a few percent (rules, enforcement, goalie equipment, shot quality), moving every player's goal expectation together; a 60-goal threshold is sensitive to a three percent level change.
nhl.league_scoring_environment.measurement: Compute league goals per team per game and PP opportunities per game to date; the season-end estimate is a precision-weighted average of the prior-season value (weight 0.6) and the to-date value with game-count weight n/(n+250); report the estimated multiplier and its sd (about 1.5 percent) and apply it as a common factor on all player and team scoring rates in simulation; refresh weekly.
raw_data: league-wide goals, games and PP counts by season and date
nhl.league_scoring_environment.why: Common scale factor for season goals; failing to model it overstates certainty across all player thresholds.

nhl.loser_point_rate.label: Loser-point and overtime-resolution rate by team
nhl.loser_point_rate.mechanism: Share of a team's games decided after regulation and its conditional win share.
nhl.loser_point_rate.rationale: Standings points include a point for an overtime or shootout loss, so two teams with equal win rates can differ in points by their extra-time frequency; regulation-win tiebreaks also depend on how often games are decided in regulation.
nhl.loser_point_rate.measurement: Per team and season compute: P(game goes beyond regulation) shrunk to league with k=30 games and 2-season weights; P(win | beyond regulation) shrunk to 0.5 with k=40 games (shootout/OT skill slight); regulation win rate from regulation results. Points per game = 2 x P(reg win) + 2 x P(extra) x p_win_extra + 1 x P(extra) x (1 - p_win_extra). Record regulation wins and ROW separately for tiebreak tracking.
raw_data: team-game result type (REG/OT/SO), points awarded, regulation wins
nhl.loser_point_rate.why: The team points threshold includes the one-point extra-time losses, which are a partly random stream, so its rate and conditional win share determine the points distribution at a given win rate.

nhl.rating_posterior_uncertainty.label: Team rating posterior uncertainty and in-season drift
nhl.rating_posterior_uncertainty.mechanism: Posterior standard deviation of each team's strength and its random-walk drift per game.
nhl.rating_posterior_uncertainty.rationale: A season or title simulation using point ratings is overconfident: the spread of true strengths and the error of the estimate both matter, and title probability is convex in rating so uncertainty raises the probability of mid-tier teams. Early-season data are noisy.
nhl.rating_posterior_uncertainty.measurement: Fit a state-space model: rating_t = rating_{t-1} + eta (sd 0.02 goals/game per game, estimated by out-of-sample likelihood), observation = score-adjusted xG differential and goal differential with measurement sd from game-level residuals; initialise with preseason prior (sd 0.25 goals/game). Output posterior mean and sd per team per day; draw ratings from the posterior in each simulation run. Re-estimate drift variance each season.
free_sources: Own computation from MoneyPuck/Natural Stat Trick game data
raw_data: team-game goals, xG, score effects, date; preseason projections
nhl.rating_posterior_uncertainty.why: Team point totals and division and streak contracts depend on rating uncertainty: ignoring the spread of true strength understates the chance of an upset in the points race and of an unexpected long streak.

nhl.stat_dist.reason: The distribution of season totals (compound count with random rate and games) decides threshold probabilities; the draft's per-game framing must be aggregated with rate uncertainty.

nhl.toi.reason: Season-long ice time projection (especially PP) scales the rate; per-game TOI must be a distribution over the remaining season, not a current value.

nhl.pp_role.reason: A PP1 slot gives a persistent rate floor; the main quantity is whether the role is secure for the season.

nhl.ixg_player.reason: Most stable estimate of goal-scoring talent for the rate; used with shrinkage because finishing is noisy.

nhl.finishing.reason: Persistent shooting talent is small relative to season noise; the shrinkage constant is the key property.

nhl.lines.reason: Line combinations change frequently over a season, so current lines carry little information for a season total beyond the role and linemate quality captured elsewhere.

nhl.linemate_quality.reason: Linemate effects are unstable over a season and partially captured by on-ice rates and PP role; evidence of persistence is weak.

nhl.career_trajectory.reason: Mislabelled secondary: with only a dozen games played the age curve and rookie/sophomore ramp are the main prior for the rest of the season.

nhl.shot_rate.reason: Mislabelled secondary: shot volume is the most stable component of goal scoring and anchors the projection, with finishing layered on top.

interactions.mechanism: A season goal total equals games played times goals per game, so uncertainty in games and in rate multiply; a 60-goal pace needs both near-full health and a high rate, so the threshold probability is much lower than the product of marginal 'pace' and 'health' intuitions.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute P(>=60) by simulation with and without games-played variability and compare with a fixed-82-game model.

interactions.mechanism: To-date goals above expected regress toward the xG-based talent, and the amount of regression depends on shots taken so far: with about 40 shots to date the prior should dominate and the to-date shooting percentage should be almost ignored.
interactions.how_to_test: Test predictive weight on to-date shooting percentage as a function of shots taken in rolling seasons.

interactions.mechanism: The league scoring multiplier applies to all players simultaneously, so thresholds on goals for different stars move together; this makes cross-player outcomes positively correlated and a common-factor error mis-prices all goal ladders in the same direction.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate year-to-year league scoring change and compare with cross-player residual correlation in goals.

interactions.mechanism: The league's longest streak is an extreme-value statistic: top teams' win probability and streakiness enter convexly, so a small rating advantage or small autocorrelation moves the probability of a 12+ game streak disproportionately.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate streak maxima under different rating spreads and autocorrelations and compare the distribution of league maxima to history.

interactions.mechanism: Division races tied on points are decided by regulation wins, so a team with fewer loser points has an advantage in ties; the effect matters only when the margin is within one or two points and interacts with remaining intra-division schedule.
interactions.how_to_test: Count division titles decided by regulation-win tiebreaks over history and compare with a points-only model.

interactions.mechanism: Age affects goals first through ice time and PP role (a regime change when a player loses PP1) before it affects shooting rate; the response is a regime switch at the role change, not a smooth decline.
interactions.how_to_test: Track PP1 membership by age and compare goal rate changes before and after loss of PP1.

nonlinearities.shape: Steep S-curve near the threshold
nonlinearities.why: Because the sd of a season goal total is about 7-8, the probability of reaching 60 moves from 10 to 60 percent as the expected total moves from 52 to 60, so a model's mean error of a few goals is a large probability error.

nonlinearities.shape: Truncated at 82 with a heavy left tail
nonlinearities.why: Games played cannot exceed 82 and the downside from injuries is a long tail; the expected value understates the cost, and the contract probability depends on the full distribution, not its mean.

nonlinearities.shape: Exponential tail in streak length
nonlinearities.why: The probability that the league's longest streak reaches length k decays roughly geometrically in k, with a rate set by the best teams' win probability; a small change in that probability changes the 12+ tail multiplicatively.
